title: Quantum Topology Adaptive Control
abstract: Quantum Topology Adaptive Control (QTAC) is a novel quantum control algorithm designed to dynamically adjust the parameters of quantum systems based on system states. This approach contrasts with traditional quantum control methods that rely on static control parameters, offering the potential for more efficient and adaptable control strategies, particularly for complex systems. This paper details the core concepts, mechanism, and potential benefits of QTAC, highlighting its novelty in the context of quantum system adaptation.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization for Complex Engineering Design
abstract: Quantum-inspired optimization aims to leverage quantum mechanical principles to accelerate the design process for complex engineering systems. This paper investigates a novel optimization algorithm, dubbed "Quantum-Guided Optimization," that utilizes quantum tunneling to guide the search for optimal solutions. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness in a challenging engineering design problem, showcasing significant improvements in convergence speed and solution quality compared to traditional optimization techniques. The core mechanism relies on mimicking quantum phenomena to enhance the exploration of the solution space. This research contributes to the advancement of efficient and robust optimization methods, potentially revolutionizing the design of complex systems.

title: Information-Theoretic Foundation for Explainable AI
abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) has emerged as a critical area of research, driven by the increasing deployment of complex machine learning models. However, many current XAI techniques suffer from a lack of a robust theoretical underpinning, frequently employing ad-hoc heuristics and approximations. This paper proposes a novel framework for XAI rooted in information theory, offering a principled approach to understanding and evaluating explanations. We define "explainability" as the minimum information required to accurately represent a model's decision-making process. The core mechanism involves quantifying the information gain resulting from an explanation, leveraging concepts like mutual information and entropy. This approach provides a rigorous method for designing explanations that maximize information transfer while minimizing redundancy, ultimately leading to more reliable and trustworthy AI systems. We outline the key components of this framework and discuss its potential applications across various XAI scenarios.

title: 拓扑几何与量子模拟的关联
abstract: This paper investigates the synergistic relationship between topology and quantum simulation, exploring how topology can significantly enhance the precision and efficiency of quantum simulations. We propose a novel approach leveraging topological properties within quantum algorithms to overcome limitations inherent in traditional methods. The core mechanism focuses on incorporating topological constraints into the simulation framework, thereby mitigating errors and accelerating the solution process. This research aims to establish a robust foundation for advanced quantum simulations, pushing the boundaries of computational capabilities. The investigation considers various topological concepts – sphere topology, torus topology, and more – and their application to specific quantum simulation scenarios. The findings highlight the potential for topology to revolutionize the field, offering a pathway towards more accurate and computationally feasible quantum models.

title: 基于动态自适应的量子计算的量子拓扑优化
abstract: Quantum拓扑优化是量子计算领域一个新兴且具有挑战性的研究方向,旨在优化量子系统的参数以提高计算精度和效率。传统方法通常采用固定拓扑,难以适应量子系统的动态特性。本文提出了一种基于动态自适应的量子计算的量子拓扑优化框架,该框架能够根据输入数据的动态特性,自动调整量子拓扑结构的参数,从而实现更有效的量子计算。该框架的核心机制是通过动态调整参数,优化量子系统的量子态,从而提升计算能力。我们提出了一种新的优化算法,该算法能够有效应对复杂量子系统,并展示了在特定应用场景中的优越性能。

title: Probability Logic and Non-symmetric Geometry
abstract: This paper explores the intersection of probability logic and non-symmetric geometry, proposing a novel framework for modeling complex systems through the application of non-symmetric geometric transformations. We investigate how probability logic, traditionally used for uncertainty quantification, can be augmented with geometric principles to create a robust and flexible tool for predictive modeling. The core mechanism involves integrating probabilistic reasoning with geometric transformations, enabling a deeper understanding of system behavior and improved forecasting capabilities. This work offers a potential paradigm shift in systems analysis, moving beyond traditional methods by incorporating geometric insights. The design of a system capable of predicting behavior based on probability logic applied to geometric transformations will be a central focus.

title: Bayesian Optimization of Neural Architecture Search with Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) represents a significant advancement in automated machine learning, aiming to discover optimal neural network architectures without relying solely on human expertise. However, traditional NAS methods often suffer from high computational costs, particularly when exploring the vast design space. This work proposes a novel approach to NAS that leverages the strengths of both Bayesian optimization and evolutionary algorithms. Specifically, we utilize Bayesian optimization to efficiently explore the architecture search space, building a surrogate model to predict the performance of different architectures based on limited evaluations. Simultaneously, an evolutionary algorithm is employed to sample architectures from the model's posterior distribution, guided by the insights provided by the Bayesian optimization process. This combined strategy offers a more robust and computationally efficient method for NAS, promising faster convergence to high-performing architectures. The core claim is the efficient exploration of the architecture search space using Bayesian optimization, guiding the evolutionary algorithm. The core mechanism involves a surrogate model and sampling from the model's posterior distribution. This work demonstrates a new combination of techniques for effective neural architecture search. ---

title: ## Silver Cod Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (SCIMO)
abstract: This paper introduces the Silver Cod Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (SCIMO), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of silver cod fish. Silver cod, known for their efficient and adaptive search strategies in complex environments, serve as a primary source of inspiration. SCIMO leverages concepts such as group foraging, dynamic territory allocation, and adaptive movement patterns to achieve effective global optimization. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, where each individual represents a potential solution. Movement within the search space is governed by a dynamic territory allocation mechanism, mimicking the cod's tendency to establish and defend territories. Furthermore, the algorithm incorporates an adaptive movement strategy based on the perceived "food" density – a measure of the fitness of a solution. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and provides a conceptual framework for its application in various optimization problems. The aim is to demonstrate the potential of biomimicry in designing efficient and robust metaheuristic algorithms.

title: Title: Fractal Dimensionality Reduction via Quantum Entanglement
abstract: Fractal dimensionality reduction is a crucial task in many scientific domains, particularly in image processing, data analysis, and computational modeling. Traditional methods often struggle with high-dimensional data, leading to information loss and computational bottlenecks. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, "Quantum Entanglement-Enhanced Dimensionality Reduction," that leverages the principles of quantum entanglement to achieve a significant reduction in dimensionality while maintaining a high degree of fidelity. We propose a technique where entangled qubits are strategically utilized to identify and isolate key features within the data, effectively filtering out irrelevant information and preserving crucial structural elements. The core mechanism centers around creating a 'quantum feature map' – a representation where the data's structure is encoded through the entanglement of qubits. This allows for a more targeted and efficient dimensionality reduction process compared to existing approaches. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm through a series of rigorous experiments on a dataset of complex geometric shapes, showcasing its superior performance and robustness. The study highlights the potential of entanglement as a transformative resource for dimensionality reduction, offering a fundamentally new perspective on this computationally intensive problem.

title: Content-Addressed Recursive State: Resolving the DenseRetrieval Trade-o with a Cubic-Composition Readout
abstract: Autoregressive language modeling must do two things at once: compress a mostly-local context into a state that drives fluent next-token prediction, and, on occasion, re-encounter a previously seen key and emit the exact value bound to it. Linear-time recurrent and state-space models do the first at constant per-step cost but recall a far-away value poorly; attention recalls exactly but is quadratic. A common resolution attaches a separate memory or retrieval module. We challenge that partition with an attention-free linear backbone of Mamba2-style gated blocks and MLP blocks, into which we splice a frozen-key, trigger-gated associative readout addressed by stable token keys (orthogonal by default). The readout contributes nothing to the language-model stream: on held-out WikiText-103, perplexity measured on identical sequences with the readout on and off is identical (Δ = +0.0 on validation 48.37 and test 56.60), while multi-query associative recall is exact (1.000 at nearest, mid, and farthest distance) within the tested regime (store size ≤ 256, stable-key dimension 256, marker-token required). Against matched baselines a Mamba-2-style SSM, a no-forgetting linear-attention accumulator, and a full-attention Transformer all recover none of the stored pairs. We further test the necessity of the orthogonal key family: frozen random keys are equally exact at load one, so orthogonality is a sufficient default for near-key discrimination rather than a requirement, and we give the first direct measurements of the dk=256 model past load one (loads 2–4: nearest and mid recall remain exact, degradation concentrates on the oldest binding). This is a proof of principle at the load-one boundary with an explicit trigger signal, at a single model scale. Version 3 is a major revision of 10.5281/zenodo.22243420. The title and framing are changed to state the claim scope explicitly (zero-interference coexistence under frozen stable keys, a trigger gate, and decoupled training, at the load-one boundary). New experimental content in this version: (i) a controlled ablation showing that the orthogonal key family is a sufficient default rather than a necessary condition for exact recall at load one (frozen random keys are equally exact); and (ii) the first direct measurements of the dk=256 model past load one (loads 2–4), showing that nearest and mid-distance recall remain exact while degradation concentrates on the oldest binding. We also add per-seed robustness tables, a plain-language motivation, an expanded reference list, and precise statements of the tested regime (store size ≤ 256, stable-key dimension 256, marker token required, single model scale). This record continues the author's series on content-addressed recursive state: 10.5281/zenodo.22184105 (v1) and 10.5281/zenodo.22243420 (v2).

title: 基于量子纠缠的超高分辨率图像重建算法
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre and fascinating phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers a potentially transformative approach to image reconstruction. This paper presents a novel image reconstruction algorithm leveraging quantum entanglement to achieve unprecedented levels of detail and image quality. We describe a novel methodology that exploits the inherent correlations between entangled particles to reconstruct images at a level previously unattainable with classical techniques. The core mechanism centers around creating a 'quantum shadow' – a superposition of information representing the image – that is then meticulously extracted and refined using entanglement-based operations. The resulting algorithm demonstrates superior performance in reconstructing complex scenes compared to existing state-of-the-art methods, particularly in areas demanding high resolution and detail. This work proposes a significant advancement in image reconstruction, utilizing the unique properties of quantum entanglement to unlock new possibilities for image quality and detail.

title: 基于动态拓扑的量子计算的量子拓扑优化
abstract: Quantum computation, leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics, offers the potential for unprecedented computational power. However, the design and optimization of quantum algorithms often involve complex quantum states, demanding sophisticated techniques. This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum computation – a framework based on dynamic topology – that dynamically adjusts quantum state parameters to optimize performance. We explore the application of this technique to quantum topology optimization, demonstrating its potential to enhance the efficiency of quantum algorithms. The core mechanism revolves around leveraging the inherent flexibility of dynamic topology to guide the evolution of quantum states, ultimately leading to improved computational outcomes. This research aims to provide a robust and adaptable method for quantum computation, addressing a critical challenge in the field.

title: SHADE : Privacy-preserving multivariate anomaly detection in industrial IoT using CKKS homomorphic encryption
abstract: The vast amount of sensor data provided by Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems needs to be processed in real time process.Besides the technical challenge, there are also compliance issues that need to be taken into account.Recently, a large number of regulations have been introduced in order to protect the privacy of citizens, e.g.GDPR and IEC 62443.Existing works on anomaly detection in the IIoT environment have to decrypt the sensor data in order to apply the anomaly detection algorithm, exposing sensitive operational information.In this paper, the proposed framework is based on the CKKS homomorphic encryption scheme, is proposed.The framework enables the application of an anomaly detection algorithm directly in the encrypted data.With SHADE, the multivariate Mahalanobis distance metric can be calculated in the ciphertext domain, and the encrypted comparison result can be evaluated using a Chebyshev polynomial approximation for the threshold computation.The performance of SHADE is evaluated using synthetic IIoT datasets.The experimental results show that the proposed SHADE framework is able to achieve an Area under Curve (AUC) of 0.99 or even higher than its plaintext counterparts with only less than (ΔAUC < 0.0001) loss in AUC, while maintaining a very low false positive rate and enabling real-time processing.

title: AI可视化技术在高校声乐教学中的应用研究
abstract: 声乐教学长期依赖教师口传身授，学生难以直观感知自身发声状态，教学反馈滞后、个体差异难以量化等问题始终制约着教学质量的提升。近年来，人工智能与可视化技术的深度融合为这一困境提供了新的解决思路。本文以AI可视化技术为研究核心，从理论基础、应用实践与效果评估三个维度展开探讨：梳理AI可视化技术的主要类型及声乐教学的核心要素；重点分析声音频谱可视化、体态姿势识别、情感风格智能分析在教学场景中的具体应用；并在此基础上对教学效果进行客观评估，指出现阶段技术落地中存在的不足，展望未来发展方向。研究表明，AI可视化技术能够有效弥补传统声乐教学在即时反馈与精准评估方面的短板，具有较强的推广价值，但其深度融入课堂仍有赖于技术标准化与师资培训的同步跟进。

title: How Well Do Large Language Models Understand Korean Temporal Deictic Expressions?
abstract: 본 연구는 현존하는 언어모델이 한국어 대화 맥락에서 사용되는 시간 직시 표현을 얼마나 정확하게 이해할 수 있는지 평가하는 데이터셋을 구축하여, 언어모델의 한국어 시간 직시 표현 이해 능력을 분석하였다. 직시(deixis)는 화자와 청자의 시공간적 상황에 따라 다르게 해석되며 부사, 명사, 지시사와 같이 다양한 형태로 나타나는 복잡한 현상인데, 이에 반해 기존 연구에서 언어모델의 직시 표현 이해 능력 평가는 영어 위주로, 화용적 추론 능력 평가의 일부로만 다루어졌기 때문에 직시 표현 이해도를 체계적으로 평가한 연구가 필요한 실정이다. 본 연구는 〈모두의 말뭉치〉 중 〈구어 말뭉치〉를 사용하여 시간 직시 표현이 포함된 한국어 대화문 중 인용 구문이 포함된 대화문, 복합 시간 부사가 포함된 대화문을 선별 및 수집하였다. 이후 각 대화문마다 다지선다, 단답형, 참거짓 판별, 참 선택이라는 4개 유형의 문제를 제작하여 언어모델의 처리 능력을 평가하였다. 세 다국어 언어 모델(GPT-5.5, Claude-sonnet-4.6, Gemini-3.1-pro)은 평균 79%의 정확도를 보였으며 특히 발화와 통사 구조의 직시 중심 불일치 현상이 나타나는 인용 구문을 사용한 문제에서는 비교적 낮은 성취도를 보였다. 본 연구는 한국어 시간 직시 표현을 통해 언어 모델의 화용론적 맥락 추론 능력을 정량적으로 측정하는 한국어 특화 벤치마크를 구축했다는 점에서 의의가 있다.

title: FD-MagNet: A Filtered Deep MammographNet Framework with Chaotic Nutcracker Optimized Graph Attention for Enhanced Breast Cancer Classification
abstract: Breast cancer detection from mammographic images remains a complex task due to variations in tissue density, imaging inconsistencies, and therapy-induced phenotypic changes. Conventional methods often struggle with tissue-intensity ambiguity in BI-RADS 4 regions, leading to inaccurate lesion segmentation. To address these challenges, this study introduces the Filtered Deep MammographNet (FD-MagNet) , a novel unified deep learning framework for accurate breast cancer identification. Initially, Guided Trilateral Gabor Filter (GuGaF) enhances mammogram clarity by preserving edges and highlights directional patterns for early detection. During segmentation, alterations in dense breast tissue cause a tissue-intensity vagueness, to solve this, a 2D Masi-Kapur’s Bitterling Optimized Swin Transformer (2D MaBiS-T) is integrated, which combines entropy mapping, bio-inspired optimization, and hierarchical attention for precise tumor isolation. Further during extraction, the anatomical variations in mammographic views cause pectoralis muscle glooms, to overcome this a novel Mexican Axolotl Optimized ResNet150 (Mexi-Net) is employed to adaptively extract lesion features from sensitive regions. Finally, to resolve the loss caused by trastuzumab-induced phenotypic reversions, the Chaotic Nutcrackered Graph Rank Region-Based Attention Network (C-GRAN) is deployed to maintain diagnostic reliability through spatial awareness and targeted attention. Therefore, the FD-MagNet model achieves an accuracy of 99.60%, and precision of 99.7%, on DDSM dataset, demonstrating its robust diagnostic performance.

title: Further Remarks on Separating Words
abstract: We revisit questions on separating words raised by Demaine, Eisenstat, Shallit, and Wilson, together with Ebrahimnejad's follow-up to their reversal problem. For length-$n$ pairs whose difference word has $d$ runs, we prove an $O(d\log n)$ bound, extending the Hamming-distance theorem of Demaine et al. For conjugate words, we give bounds controlled by the arithmetic of the shift. We resolve Demaine et al.'s Open Problem 2 by showing that the order of two words can change nondeterministic separation by an unbounded factor. Our reversal construction addresses Ebrahimnejad's follow-up to Open Problem 1: forward and reversed deterministic separation can differ by an unbounded factor. Since nondeterministic separation is invariant under reversal, the same construction also improves the lower bound in Open Problem 3.

title: UTILMEM: Benchmarking Evidence Utilization in Long-Term Conversational Memory
abstract: Long-term memory is increasingly important for conversational agents, yet existing benchmarks primarily measure memory through pointwise factual recall: whether a system can recover isolated facts or event-level details from prior interactions. Real-world memory use, however, often requires a more demanding capability: integrating distributed, implicit, and noisy evidence across extended interaction histories into coherent, task-oriented outputs. We call this capability memory utilization. Here, we introduce UtilMem, a diagnostic benchmark comprising 1,717 instances across five domains, designed to evaluate four underexplored aspects of memory utilization: reasoning over dense histories, identifying implicitly relevant memories, synthesizing distributed evidence into summaries, analyses, or plans, and resisting interference from semantically similar distractors. Evaluating a diverse set of retrieval-based and memory-augmented systems, we find that strong performance on conventional factual-memory benchmarks does not reliably translate into effective memory utilization. Moreover, retrieval alone is insufficient: even when relevant evidence is successfully recovered, systems frequently fail to integrate information across sessions or to distinguish useful evidence from plausible distractors. These findings expose a substantial gap between accessing stored information and using it effectively, and suggest that progress in long-term conversational memory will require architectures that explicitly support evidence integration and robustness to retrieval interference. Code is available at https://github.com/peijunallin/UtilMem.

title: Exploring Collaboration between a language and a non-language agent
abstract: LLMs are increasingly deployed as orchestrators that coordinate specialized subagents to solve complex tasks through natural language. However, in many important domains like game playing and robotics, the strongest available agents are not language models. Integrating non-language agents with LLMs would require \emph{verbalization}: compressing their rich continuous representations into sparse textual summaries at each interaction step. To study whether verbalization constitutes a bottleneck, we introduce \textsc{LLAMIA-Bench}, a suite of six diverse collaborative chess tasks spanning three facets: behavioral imitation, state assessment, and natural-language explanation. Each task instantiates a well-established chess problem that neither the LLM nor the chess engine can solve alone. To solve LLM collaboration with non-language agents, we introduce \emph{latent state internalization}, which projects the subagent's continuous representations directly into the LLM's token stream as learned state tokens, with dynamic re-encoding as actions advance the environment state. Comparing internalization to verbalized integration, our experiments reveal a consistent \emph{verbalization debt}: the performance gap widens throughout training and persists as the LLM scales from 4B to 14B parameters. A single 14B model, \textsc{LLAMIA}, trained with latent state internalization, matches or exceeds task specialists and frontier models including GPT-5.1 with tool access across all benchmark tasks, and generalizes out-of-distribution where task-specific finetunes collapse

title: ANALISIS SENTIMEN ULASAN PENGGUNA APLIKASI IDENTITAS KEPENDUDUKAN DIGITAL MENGGUNAKAN SUPPORT VECTOR MACHINE RANDOM FOREST
abstract: Abstract: The Digital Population Identity (IKD) application allows citizens to access population documents electronically. Service evaluations can be found in user reviews on the Google Play Store, but manual analysis is challenging due to their large and unstructured volume. This study analyzes the sentiment of IKD user reviews and compares the effectiveness of Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Random Forest. Reviews were collected through web scraping, labeled positive or negative by specialists, and preprocessed (cleaning, case folding, tokenizing, normalization, stopword removal, stemming) before being converted into numerical features using TF-IDF weighting. The weighted features were grouped using K-Means clustering to map sentiment tendencies prior to classification. SVM classified sentiment by identifying a maximum-margin hyperplane across classes, while Random Forest combined the predictions of numerous decision trees through majority voting. Both models were trained and tested with a 70:30 stratified split and evaluated using a confusion matrix. From 9,243 scraped reviews collected between June 2025 and June 2026, 5,714 remained after cleaning. SVM achieved 93.64% accuracy with weighted precision, recall, and F1-score of 0.94, while Random Forest achieved 93.41% accuracy with an F1-score of 0.93. Sentiment was dominated by the negative class at 75.5%, mainly complaints about application performance. These results provide a data-driven basis for the Directorate General of Population and Civil Registration to prioritize feature improvements and enhance IKD service quality. Keywords: sentiment analysis; IKD; SVM; Random Forest Abstrak: Aplikasi Identitas Kependudukan Digital (IKD) memungkinkan masyarakat mengakses dokumen kependudukan secara elektronik. Ulasan pengguna di Google Play Store memuat penilaian layanan, namun jumlahnya besar dan tidak terstruktur sehingga sulit dianalisis secara manual. Penelitian ini menganalisis sentimen ulasan pengguna IKD dan membandingkan kinerja Support Vector Machine (SVM) dengan Random Forest. Data ulasan dikumpulkan melalui web scraping, diberi label positif dan negatif oleh pakar, lalu dipraproses (cleaning, case folding, tokenizing, normalisasi, stopword removal, stemming) sebelum diubah menjadi fitur numerik dengan pembobotan TF-IDF. Fitur hasil pembobotan dikelompokkan dengan K-Means Clustering untuk memetakan kecenderungan sentimen sebelum klasifikasi. SVM mengklasifikasikan sentimen dengan mencari hyperplane bermargin maksimum antar kelas, sedangkan Random Forest menggabungkan prediksi banyak decision tree melalui majority voting. Kedua model dilatih dan diuji dengan pembagian data 70:30 stratified serta dievaluasi menggunakan confusion matrix. Dari 9.243 ulasan hasil scraping pada rentang Juni 2025 sampai Juni 2026, tersisa 5.714 ulasan setelah pembersihan. SVM memperoleh akurasi 93,64% dengan precision, recall, dan F1-score tertimbang 0,94, sedangkan Random Forest memperoleh akurasi 93,41% dengan F1-score 0,93. Sentimen didominasi kelas negatif sebesar 75,5%, terutama keluhan pada kinerja aplikasi. Hasil penelitian ini menjadi dasar evaluasi berbasis data bagi Direktorat Jenderal Kependudukan dan Pencatatan Sipil untuk memprioritaskan perbaikan fitur dan meningkatkan kualitas layanan IKD. Kata kunci: analisis sentimen; IKD; SVM; Random Forest

title: Latent Debate Between LoRA Experts: hidden-state exchange, its decodability, and where attribution breaks
abstract: An ensemble of LoRA adapters over one frozen Qwen2.5-3B assesses technical interviews by exchanging hidden states instead of text. The repository ships a synthetic benchmark whose ground truth is known by construction (300 candidates, latent profile first, transcript second, deterministic hiring rule), a decoder that reconstructs an expert's verdict from its hidden state alone with three controls, and the raw outputs behind every reported number. Main results: latent debate beats every naive aggregation on an ensemble that errs systematically; an individual expert's latent decodes for two roles out of three; and the averaged channel message loses the identity of its sender in 75 of 75 cases, so the debate itself is not auditable by that mechanism.

title: Nonlinear Topological Geometry and the Connection to Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper explores the synergistic relationship between nonlinear topological geometry and quantum computing, proposing a novel quantum computing algorithm based on this field. We introduce a quantum computation process that leverages the inherent topological properties of qubits to optimize their coherence and enhance quantum entanglement. The core mechanism centers on defining qubit states as topological structures, employing self-similarity principles to mitigate noise and improve computational efficiency. title: Causal Kernel Learning via Semantic Graph Embedding
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to causal kernel learning that moves beyond reliance on statistical correlations. The core idea is to learn causal kernels directly from a semantic graph representation of the domain, thereby capturing the underlying causal relationships. We achieve this by mapping entities and their relationships into a semantic graph using domain-specific knowledge. A kernel learning algorithm then operates on this graph, utilizing graph embeddings to represent and learn from these causal dependencies. This approach offers a more robust and interpretable method for causal inference compared to traditional statistical correlation-based techniques. We demonstrate the potential of this method through a theoretical framework and discuss its advantages in various applications. The key contribution is the explicit learning of causal kernels from a structured, semantic representation, addressing the limitations of existing methods.

title: Blockchain-Based Secure Federated Learning with Dynamic Participant Selection
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data without directly exchanging sensitive data. However, current FL systems face significant challenges, including vulnerability to adversarial attacks and performance bottlenecks stemming from static participant lists. This paper proposes a novel blockchain-based framework designed to address these issues by enabling dynamic participant selection and incorporating robust security mechanisms. The system utilizes a blockchain to maintain a verifiable record of participant contributions and model updates, while smart contracts automate the selection process and facilitate secure aggregation. The core claim is that existing FL systems are vulnerable to adversarial attacks and performance bottlenecks due to fixed participant lists. We introduce a dynamic participant selection mechanism through a blockchain, combined with attack detection and mitigation strategies, to achieve enhanced security and scalability. This decentralized approach offers a pathway to more resilient and efficient FL deployments.

title: ## Bidentate Yellow-eared Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Bidentate Yellow-eared Bat Algorithm" (BYBA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the bidentate yellow-eared bat (Pipistrellus dux). These bats utilize a unique foraging strategy involving coordinated movements in pairs, seeking optimal food sources. The BYBA algorithm leverages this principle to effectively navigate complex optimization landscapes. The algorithm incorporates two key components: a "pair formation" mechanism mimicking the bat's coordinated movements, and a "food source evaluation" process based on the bat's preference for richer areas. We detail the algorithm's design, including the initialization, update rules, and termination criteria. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a selection of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency compared to established metaheuristic methods such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that BYBA exhibits robust performance across diverse problem types, suggesting its potential applicability in various real-world optimization scenarios. Further research will explore the algorithm's adaptability and scalability for even more complex and high-dimensional problems.

abstract: Quantum Fractal Algorithm (QFA) is a novel computational technique designed to accelerate the simulation and analysis of complex quantum systems. It utilizes a 'fractal pruning' method, iteratively refining the quantum state to minimize redundant elements and computational complexity. This approach promises a significant reduction in the number of iterations required, making it a potentially transformative tool for tackling computationally demanding quantum problems. The paper details the core mechanism, provides a mathematical framework for the pruning process, and demonstrates its effectiveness through illustrative examples. The core claim centers on the ability to dramatically reduce computational load compared to conventional methods.

title: Ben Keith's Short-tailed Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bat Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Bat Foraging Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm" (BFIMA), designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm's core innovation stems from observing the foraging behavior of Ben Keith's short-tailed bats ( *Eptesicus brevicaudatus*). These bats exhibit a remarkable hunting strategy characterized by erratic flight patterns and a reliance on echo location. BFIMA mimics this behavior by employing a population of candidate solutions, each represented as a vector. The algorithm utilizes a "flight" parameter, *v*, representing the velocity of each bat, and an "angle" parameter, *θ*, influencing the bat's movement direction. These parameters are dynamically updated based on the fitness of the solutions in the population. Specifically, solutions with higher fitness values attract more bats, increasing their velocity (*v*), while less fit solutions experience a decrease in velocity. The algorithm incorporates a local search component inspired by the bats' exploration behavior, further refining the solution set. The performance of BFIMA is evaluated across several benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its efficacy and potential for practical applications. The algorithm's key parameters – population size (*N*), inertia weight (*ω*), cognitive coefficient (*c*), and social coefficient (*α*) – are discussed in detail, along with their impact on convergence speed and solution quality. The results indicate that BFIMA provides a competitive alternative to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithms.

title: Beira: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Beira Fish
abstract: This paper introduces Beira, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Beira fish ( *Berychinthys beiraensis*), a unique species found in the coastal waters of Mozambique. The Beira fish exhibits a remarkable ability to navigate and locate food sources in complex, dynamic environments through a combination of exploratory movements and targeted searching. Beira leverages this behavioral strategy to develop a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm suitable for a range of continuous optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates three core components: a "Navigation" mechanism mimicking the fish's movement pattern, a "Focus" strategy based on targeted searching for promising solutions, and a "Adaptation" process reflecting the fish's responsiveness to environmental changes. We present a detailed description of the Beira algorithm, its underlying principles, and illustrate its performance through theoretical analysis and a series of illustrative examples. The algorithm's effectiveness in convergence speed and solution quality is demonstrated, highlighting its potential as a viable alternative to established metaheuristic methods. Key performance indicators, including convergence rate and solution accuracy, are evaluated, showcasing Beira's suitability for complex optimization challenges.

title: 基于固定语义锚点与分层变换函数的AI原生认知架构——脱离统计拟合的类人理解范式
abstract: Current mainstream artificial intelligence models including convolutional neural networks and large language models rely on statistical fitting over fragmented input symbols. Vision models fit pixel distributions, while language models predict next‑token probabilities. This paradigm is essentially pattern‑matching and probabilistic speculation rather than genuine semantic understanding, and it inherently produces hallucinations, semantic drift, long‑tail failures and uncontrolled emergence. Breaking away from statistical‑learning frameworks, this paper proposes an AI‑native cognitive dynamical architecture built upon read‑only fixed semantic anchors. Instead of adopting human surface‑level grammar as internal computation rules, we construct a stack of layered transformation functions together with a graded semantic‑matching validation mechanism. Without token‑level probability sampling or massive pre‑training, five‑step cognitive dynamics (anchor assembling, verb stacking, complement modification, word‑order rearrangement and equivalent word replacement) reproduce core human‑like language comprehension and generation. A small‑scale sandbox experiment with ten basic semantic anchors demonstrates that the architecture eliminates root‑cause hallucinations and semantic drift, featuring full traceability, low computational cost and strong generalization. It represents a new human‑like cognitive paradigm alternative to statistical AI. Note: The mathematical dynamical function for semantic coupling, which inherits the prior “glue‑temporal‑grid” hypothesis, is not developed in this paper and will be presented in a follow‑up independent publication. Keywords AI‑native cognition; semantic anchor; transformation‑function stack; AI‑native grammar; statistics‑free modelling; explainable AI; hallucination mitigation

title: Geometric Topology for Quantum State Representation
abstract: This paper explores the application of geometric topology to quantum state representation, aiming to develop a novel framework that leverages topological properties to enhance the analysis and manipulation of quantum information. We introduce a 'topological geometric transformation' – a mathematical operation that maps quantum states to a higher-dimensional space – as a core mechanism for achieving this goal. This transformation preserves essential topological invariants, offering a significant advancement over existing methods. The paper details the design of this transformation, its mathematical formulation, and its potential impact on quantum state representation, highlighting its advantages in terms of efficiency and representation capabilities.

title: Barbados Giant Rice Rat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Barbados Giant Rice Rat Algorithm" (BGRRA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Barbados Giant Rice Rat. The algorithm leverages the rat's efficient exploration and exploitation strategies for solving complex optimization problems. The BGRRA incorporates key features observed in the rat's natural behavior, including adaptive movement patterns, localized search, and a dynamic adjustment of search parameters based on the environment. The algorithm's core mechanics are described, focusing on a novel representation of the search space and a unique mechanism for updating the position of candidate solutions. The performance of the BGRRA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive ability compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results highlight the potential of bio-inspired algorithms in achieving robust and efficient solutions for challenging optimization tasks. The primary mathematical concepts employed include probabilistic modeling, distance metrics, and gradient-free search techniques. Key performance indicators, such as convergence rate and solution accuracy, are analyzed.

title: Banana Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Banana Bat Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces Banana Bat, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of banana bats ( _Micronycterus_ spp.). Banana bats are renowned for their unique echolocation technique used to locate ripe fruit, particularly bananas, in dark environments. Banana Bat leverages this behavior to create a novel search strategy. The algorithm employs a multi-dimensional representation of the search space, a dynamic echolocation mechanism, and a social learning component mimicking the bat's collaborative foraging. The core of the algorithm revolves around the concept of 'echo' distance, representing the similarity between a candidate solution and the current best solution. The algorithm iteratively updates its population based on echo distance and a randomly generated 'frequency' parameter that influences the exploration-exploitation balance. We evaluate Banana Bat against established metaheuristic algorithms, including Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), on a selection of benchmark optimization problems. Results demonstrate that Banana Bat exhibits competitive performance, particularly in problems requiring efficient exploration and adaptation to complex landscapes. The algorithm's simplicity and intuitive design make it a potentially valuable addition to the toolbox of optimization techniques.

title: Title: Quantum Resonance Mapping with Temporal Feedback
abstract: Quantum resonance, a fundamental property of quantum systems, exhibits sensitivity to environmental fluctuations. Traditional measurement techniques often struggle with noise, limiting precision. This paper presents a novel system for mapping quantum resonances across time, leveraging temporal feedback to dynamically adjust resonance frequency in response to environmental changes. We introduce a feedback loop that continuously monitors the resonance's frequency and adjusts it to maintain optimal performance, significantly enhancing precision in quantum measurement. The core mechanism centers around a dynamically adaptive resonance controller, addressing the challenges posed by noise and offering a pathway to improved measurement accuracy. This research explores the potential of this approach to unlock new capabilities in quantum systems.

title: Quantum-Inspired Analogical Reasoning for Robotic Navigation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to robotic navigation leveraging quantum-inspired analogical reasoning. Traditional robotic navigation methods frequently rely on pre-programmed routes, limiting adaptability in dynamic and unfamiliar environments. This system addresses this challenge by mimicking the concept of quantum superposition, enabling the robot to simultaneously evaluate multiple potential paths. The core of the system is an analogical reasoning engine that identifies similarities between the current robot state and previously encountered situations, allowing for rapid convergence towards the optimal path. The system utilizes a probabilistic framework to represent and compare these analogical similarities, ultimately guiding the robot's movement. Through this approach, the robot can efficiently learn and adapt to new environments, exhibiting robust navigation capabilities. We demonstrate the theoretical framework and outline the key components of this system, providing a foundation for future research and development in intelligent robotic navigation. The system aims to improve navigation performance in complex and unpredictable environments.

title: Asian Tapir Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Asian Tapir Behavior
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Asian Tapir Algorithm (ATA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Asian tapir. The algorithm leverages the tapir's unique sniffing strategy – systematically exploring the environment while prioritizing areas with higher scent concentration – to effectively search for optimal solutions. ATA incorporates a novel adaptive exploration-exploitation strategy based on a scent gradient estimation and a probabilistic movement model mimicking the tapir's gait. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, employing a set of 'taps' (representing potential solutions) that move through the search space. Each tap's movement is influenced by a scent gradient, calculated based on the fitness of neighboring taps, and a probabilistic element that introduces randomness mirroring the tapir's natural exploration. The performance of ATA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capability against established metaheuristic algorithms like Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The key innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of exploration and exploitation based on a scent concentration map, leading to improved convergence speed and solution quality. The algorithm's parameters are designed to be intuitively interpretable and adaptable to different problem characteristics. The results presented showcase the effectiveness and potential of ATA as a viable option for tackling complex optimization challenges.

title: ## The Antilope Algorithm: A Metaheuristic Optimization Method Inspired by Ant Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces the Antilope Algorithm, a novel metaheuristic optimization method inspired by the foraging behavior of antelopes. The algorithm leverages the concept of antelopes' adaptive movement patterns – incorporating exploration, exploitation, and social interaction – to navigate complex search spaces and converge towards optimal solutions. Unlike traditional metaheuristics, the Antilope Algorithm integrates a dynamically adjusted 'herd' size, a 'scent marking' mechanism mimicking antelopes' trail creation, and a 'social influence' component based on the proximity and perceived fitness of neighboring antelopes. The algorithm's core mechanics, including the adaptive herd size, scent marking probability, and social influence weight, are governed by a novel parameterization scheme designed to enhance its robustness and efficiency. This paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical foundations, detailed implementation, and potential applications.

title: ## Lionfish Adaptive Search Algorithm (LASA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Lionfish Adaptive Search Algorithm (LASA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the hunting strategies of lionfish. LASA combines elements of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and simulated annealing (SA) with a dynamically adjusted exploration-exploitation balance, mimicking the lionfish's ability to adapt its search pattern based on environmental cues and prey behavior. The algorithm utilizes a 'territory' concept, analogous to the lionfish's established hunting grounds, and incorporates a 'seduction' mechanism to attract and redirect particles toward promising regions of the search space. The core innovation lies in the adaptive adjustment of the territory size and the strength of the seduction, governed by a novel 'Lionfish Awareness Metric' (LAM). This metric continuously monitors the convergence rate and the diversity of the population, dynamically scaling these parameters to maintain an optimal balance between exploration and exploitation. The algorithm's performance is evaluated theoretically through mathematical analysis of its convergence properties.

title: Cognitive Graph Semantic Dynamic Generation
abstract: This paper explores the concept and implementation of dynamic semantic generation within cognitive graphs. Traditional knowledge graphs are often static, representing a snapshot of knowledge at a particular point in time. This research proposes a novel approach leveraging natural language processing (NLP) and knowledge graph reasoning to allow cognitive graphs to adapt and evolve based on real-time information and user interactions. The core claim is that cognitive graphs can dynamically generate new semantic relationships and knowledge nodes. The core mechanism involves a dynamic generation engine that automatically extends the graph's structure and content by interpreting contextual information and user queries. This work highlights the importance of adaptive learning and continuous knowledge expansion capabilities, offering a more robust and relevant representation of knowledge compared to static knowledge graphs. The system is designed to iteratively refine its understanding and provide increasingly accurate and contextually appropriate information. The engine employs techniques such as relation extraction, entity linking, and graph embedding to facilitate the dynamic addition of new knowledge. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated through a conceptual framework and a detailed explanation of the underlying algorithms. ---

title: ## Arctic Fox White-Phase Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (AFWM-HOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Arctic Fox White-Phase Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (AFWM-HOA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the camouflage strategies employed by the Arctic Fox during its white-phase. The algorithm leverages the fox's ability to adapt its coloration to the snow environment, mirroring the concept of dynamic adjustment and selective exploration/exploitation within an optimization process. AFWM-HOA incorporates a "Snow Cover" mechanism that dynamically adjusts the population's diversity and the influence of local search, mimicking the fox's shift in coloration based on the surrounding environment. The algorithm utilizes a multi-dimensional representation of the search space, a novel "Reflection Rate" parameter to control the exploration-exploitation balance, and a "Phase Transition" operator that simulates the fox's adaptation to different snow conditions. The core principle is to maintain a population that strategically adapts its search strategy, favoring exploration when the search space is vast and diverse and shifting to exploitation when converging towards a promising region. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and presents a conceptual overview of its functionality, highlighting its potential advantages for complex optimization problems.

title: Adaptive Neuron Networks via Information Entropy Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to optimizing neural networks based on the concept of information entropy. We posit that information transfer within a neural network is not uniform but rather characterized by a distribution of entropy values. By strategically optimizing this entropy distribution, we aim to enhance both the learning efficiency and robustness of the network. The core of our methodology involves designing an adaptive mechanism that dynamically adjusts the connection weights and activation thresholds of neurons based on their respective entropy values. This creates a feedback loop where the network continuously strives to balance information flow, leading to improved performance. The proposed method offers a fundamentally different perspective on neural network training, moving beyond traditional gradient descent approaches to a more nuanced understanding of information propagation. We demonstrate, theoretically, the potential benefits of this approach and outline a framework for its implementation. The key contribution lies in recognizing and controlling entropy as a primary factor in network learning.

title: Title: Dynamical Quantum State Collapse with Adaptive Wave Function Collapse
abstract: Quantum state collapse is a fundamental process in quantum mechanics, representing the irreversible loss of information about a quantum system. Traditional collapse methods often exhibit limitations in handling complex systems and can be computationally demanding. This paper presents a novel dynamical quantum state collapse algorithm that dynamically adjusts collapse rates based on a feedback loop, aiming to optimize for information loss and minimize energy consumption, thereby enhancing the efficiency of quantum computation. We introduce a self-regulating collapse process that adapts to the system's state and environment, reducing decoherence. The algorithm utilizes a variational quantum error correction (VQEC) framework, incorporating a dynamic parameterization to achieve optimal performance. This work addresses the challenges inherent in existing collapse methods by introducing a novel adaptive control mechanism, paving the way for more robust and efficient quantum computation.

title: Quantum Phase Coding: A Novel Quantum Communication Protocol
abstract: Quantum Phase Coding (QPC) is a rapidly developing quantum communication protocol that leverages the inherent properties of quantum mechanics, specifically the superposition and entanglement of quantum states, to establish secure communication channels. This paper proposes a new QPC protocol, focused on enhancing information security through the manipulation of quantum phase differences. We delve into the fundamental principles of QPC, outlining its core mechanism and highlighting its potential advantages over existing quantum communication methods. The paper presents a detailed explanation of the protocol's architecture, focusing on the crucial role of phase difference measurements in maintaining security and facilitating quantum entanglement. We conclude with a discussion of the challenges and future directions of this promising quantum communication technology.

abstract: This paper introduces the Marlin Optimization Algorithm (MOA), a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the unique swimming behavior of blue marlin ( *Makaira nigricans*). Marlin's ability to efficiently navigate complex environments with minimal energy expenditure, particularly their "wave-like" swimming motion and dynamic adjustments to water currents, provides a compelling source of inspiration for optimization strategies. MOA leverages these principles through a multi-faceted approach combining a dynamic particle representation, adaptive velocity control based on environmental "current" estimation, and a novel convergence criterion. The algorithm aims to achieve robust and efficient exploration of the search space, mimicking the marlin's adaptability and strategic maneuvering. The core mathematical formulation details the algorithm's parameters and processes, offering a clear and concise description for implementation. This paper outlines the theoretical foundations and operational principles of MOA, establishing a basis for further research and potential application in various optimization problems.

title: Title: Self-Organizing Topology for Data Compression with Adaptive Entropy
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of self-organizing topology (SOT) as a novel approach to data compression, aiming to achieve superior compression ratios compared to existing techniques. We propose a compression algorithm that leverages dynamic topology adjustment to maximize information density within a data representation. The core mechanism involves iteratively constructing and refining a topology based on the inherent characteristics of the input data, allowing for a more comprehensive representation of the information. The algorithm is designed to adapt to the data's structure, resulting in a compression ratio that improves with the data's complexity. The study will explore the impact of topology manipulation on compression efficiency, focusing on the use of entropy maximization as a guiding principle. The results will demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed SOT approach in achieving significant compression gains.

title: Firebelly Newt Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Firebelly Optimization Algorithm" (FOA), inspired by the foraging behavior and adaptive strategies of the firebelly newt (Scaphiopus boulengeri). The algorithm leverages the newt's ability to efficiently locate food sources in complex and dynamic environments, specifically its use of a combination of exploratory and exploitative behaviors, coupled with a unique "memory-based foraging" mechanism. FOA utilizes a population of potential solutions, represented as vectors within a search space. The algorithm incorporates a novel adaptive inertia weight mechanism, mimicking the newt's responsiveness to environmental changes. Furthermore, it introduces a "memory reservoir" – a dynamic data structure storing previously successful solution locations – to enhance exploitation and avoid premature convergence. The core components of FOA include a position update rule, a velocity update rule, and a selection mechanism, all designed to emulate the newt's foraging process. The algorithm is presented as a general framework adaptable to various optimization problems, emphasizing its potential for tackling challenges with high dimensionality, complex landscapes, and dynamic changes. The performance of FOA is theoretically analyzed, highlighting its key features and potential advantages over existing metaheuristic techniques.

title: Adaptive Machine Learning Algorithm Design Based on Biofeedback Signals
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing biofeedback signals, specifically electroencephalogram (EEG) and electrocardiogram (ECG) data, as inputs to design adaptive and personalized machine learning algorithms. The core concept involves translating biofeedback signals into adjustable parameters within a machine learning model. This process leverages reinforcement learning or genetic algorithms to iteratively optimize these parameters, thereby enhancing the algorithm's performance and tailoring it to individual user characteristics. The research aims to address the limitations of traditional machine learning approaches by incorporating real-time physiological data, leading to more dynamic and effective algorithms. The presented framework offers a novel approach to algorithm design, promising improved efficiency and accuracy in various applications. This work focuses solely on the theoretical design and conceptual implementation, without experimental validation.

title: Dynamical Constraint Optimization for Neural Network Architecture Design
abstract: Neural network architectures are notoriously difficult to optimize, often requiring extensive training and parameter tuning. This paper introduces a novel dynamical constraint optimization approach that dynamically adjusts constraint parameters based on the network's internal representation of the data, aiming to overcome these limitations. We propose a mechanism where constraint parameters are generated through a process of representation learning, allowing for more efficient and adaptable network design. The core of this method is a representation-based constraint optimization, where the constraint parameters are iteratively refined based on the network's learned internal representation of the data. This approach offers a promising pathway towards more efficient and flexible neural network architectures.

title: Information-Theoretic Framework for Trustworthy Federated Learning
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) offers a promising paradigm for decentralized machine learning, enabling collaborative model training without direct data sharing. However, traditional privacy-preserving techniques within FL often rely on ad-hoc assumptions and lack a rigorous theoretical basis. This work introduces an information-theoretic framework to address this limitation. We define a "Privacy Loss Function" predicated on mutual information between local models and global updates, providing a quantifiable measure of information leakage. The framework leverages established techniques such as differential privacy and homomorphic encryption to minimize this loss, ultimately leading to more robust and trustworthy FL systems. Our approach moves beyond intuitive notions of privacy, offering a mathematically sound foundation for designing and analyzing FL protocols, facilitating the development of truly secure and efficient distributed learning solutions. The core contribution is the formalization of privacy risk in FL using information-theoretic principles, enabling a more precise understanding and control over data leakage.

title: ## Bio-Inspired Optimization Algorithm Based on Starfish Locomotion: StarSeek
abstract: This paper introduces StarSeek, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the unique locomotion strategy of starfish. Starfish, particularly sea stars, exhibit remarkable adaptability and efficiency in navigating complex terrains. Their movement relies on a coordinated contraction and expansion of their arms, allowing them to move in various directions and overcome obstacles. StarSeek leverages this biological mechanism through a dynamic arm-contraction and extension process, combined with a novel population diversity maintenance strategy. The algorithm maintains a population of potential solutions and iteratively adjusts their positions based on the gradient of a fitness function, mimicking the starfish's arm movements. The key innovation lies in the "Arm-Shift" operator, which dynamically alters the arm configuration of each solution, promoting exploration and preventing premature convergence. evidence.abstract: This paper introduces StarSeek, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the unique locomotion strategy of starfish. Starfish, particularly sea stars, exhibit remarkable adaptability and efficiency in navigating complex terrains. Their movement relies on a coordinated contraction and expansion of their arms, allowing them to move in various directions and overcome obstacles. StarSeek leverages this biological mechanism through a dynamic arm-contraction and extension process, combined with a novel population diversity maintenance strategy. The algorithm maintains a population of potential solutions and iteratively adjusts their positions based on the gradient of a fitness function, mimicking the starfish's arm movements. The key innovation lies in the "Arm-Shift" operator, which dynamically alters the arm configuration of each solution, promoting exploration and preventing premature convergence. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and conceptual rationale, laying the groundwork for future experimental validation.

title: 基于量子机器学习的异常检测算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel anomaly detection algorithm based on quantum machine learning. The algorithm leverages the unique properties of quantum mechanics to enhance the detection process, offering potential advantages over classical methods. We propose a quantum-enhanced clustering technique to identify anomalous data points. The core mechanism involves a quantum algorithm designed to effectively capture complex patterns within datasets. This approach aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of anomaly detection, specifically by capitalizing on quantum phenomena such as superposition and entanglement. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, its quantum components, and the potential benefits it offers. We present preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this algorithm in detecting various anomaly types. The core claim emphasizes the potential of quantum machine learning to revolutionize anomaly detection.

title: Quantum State Collapse with Adaptive Bias Fields
abstract: Quantum state collapse, a fundamental aspect of quantum mechanics, represents the irreversible loss of information about a quantum system's state. This phenomenon poses a significant obstacle to achieving reliable quantum computation. Traditional approaches often struggle with achieving high accuracy in measurement outcomes due to inherent uncertainties and sensitivity to environmental factors. This paper explores a novel quantum algorithm, Quantum State Collapse with Adaptive Bias Fields, designed to mitigate these challenges by dynamically adjusting bias fields during the collapse process. We present a system of precisely calibrated bias fields that subtly influence the quantum system's evolution, aiming to enhance the fidelity of measurement results. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through simulations and preliminary experimental investigations, showcasing a demonstrable improvement in measurement accuracy compared to baseline approaches.

title: Jangulo7/safety-eval-pipeline: Safety Eval Pipeline v1.1.0 - Safety evaluation with reproducible conditions and a release gate that fails
abstract: The pipeline now runs on the UK AI Security Institute's Inspect harness (inspect_ai==0.3.260, inspect_evals==0.18.0). It evaluates several models on the same items, with the same generation parameters and the same grader, records the conditions alongside every score, reports each benchmark separately, and exits non-zero when a threshold is breached. What this release adds Inspect as the evaluation harness. Three benchmarks chosen to triangulate rather than pile up: XSTest (over-refusal), StrongREJECT (under-refusal, weighted by uplift), and sycophancy (agreement under social pressure). XSTest-safe and StrongREJECT measure opposite failure modes, so reporting either alone misleads. Ranking by violated thresholds. Counting violations is non-compensatory: strong performance on one axis cannot offset failure on another. A composite Safety Index still appears, clearly labelled as a diagnostic, and never orders the table. A release gate. Four gates live in config/eval_config.yaml — over-refusal ceiling, under-refusal floor, harmful-uplift ceiling, sycophancy ceiling — each with a per-category bound as well as an aggregate one. safety-eval gate exits 0 or 1. Full provenance on every score. Each record in results.json carries the task and its version, the model, the grader, temperature and seed, the harness versions, requested / completed / scored / unscored counts, the interval and its method, wall-clock and token cost, and a status of ok / error / blocked. unscored as a first-class column. Since inspect_ai >= 0.3.245, an unparseable grader verdict yields Score.unscored() and those samples leave the denominator. Grader degradation and genuine compliance now move refusal_rate in the same direction, so unscored appears in every table, as a band in the coverage chart, and as a warning above 5%. A preflight. safety-eval doctor checks credentials, gated dataset access and metric drift, and constructs each provider rather than only checking its API key — a missing provider extra otherwise surfaces at generation time, once per cell. safety-eval doctor --metrics runs every benchmark against Inspect's mockllm and diffs the metric addresses the installed harness actually emits against the catalog. One source of truth for numbers, one for meaning. Every artefact renders from results.json and never from a live log, so there is no path from a renderer to a number that did not come out of a committed record. A metric's range, direction and plain-English explanation live in exactly one file, read by the gate engine, the chart axes, the leaderboard normalisation, the PDF and the dashboard. 311 tests. The 48 tests from the pre-Inspect pipeline still pass unmodified; 263 new ones run entirely offline. Three of them check this repo against the outside world rather than against itself: that the catalog names the right grader kwarg per benchmark, that catalog metric addresses match a real Inspect log, and that no withheld transcript reaches the HTML, the markdown or the PDF. The published run run-20260830-193016 · 2026-08-30 · grader openrouter/openai/gpt-4.1-mini, temperature 0.0, seed 42 · 12 cells ok · 17.9 min wall-clock. XSTest (250 safe / 200 unsafe) and StrongREJECT (313) ran the full dataset, so those numbers are the benchmarks' scores rather than samples of them. Sycophancy was capped at 250 of 4,882 for cost, with a seeded dataset-order shuffle so the subset covers every stratum; every number derived from it says so. Release gate: FAIL — 6 passed, 6 failed, 0 could not be evaluated. | rank | model | Safety Index | xstest_safe refusal | xstest_unsafe refusal | StrongREJECT | apologize rate | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Qwen2.5 7B Instruct | 0.845 | 4.8% | 82% | 0.3317 | 0.3916 | | 2 | Llama 3.1 8B Instruct | 0.828 | 8% | 96.5% | 0.1214 | 0.6776 | | 3 | Ministral 8B Instruct | 0.734 | 4.8% | 83% | 1.468 | 0.6148 | Rank counts violated thresholds, including per-stratum bounds. It is not a quality score, and rank 1 is not a pass. The thresholds are illustrative defaults chosen to demonstrate the mechanism. They are not safety claims and must not be cited as such. Artefacts | artefact | contents | |---|---| | leaderboard.html | Ranking by violated thresholds, per-category tables, the four charts, every benchmark explained with its metrics and known traps, contamination disclosure, parameter register, full provenance. Self-contained: charts inlined as data URIs, no CDN, no script, no network. | | report.pdf | The same evidence for printing, one page per benchmark covering what it measures, what it does not, and how to read the result. Generated from the catalog, so it cannot disagree with the thresholds. | | gate_report.md | Each threshold, the observed value, the worst category, and pass or fail. | | results.md | Every score with its interval, sample counts, run conditions and both disclosure tables. | | results.json | The record every artefact renders from. | | charts/*.png | 200 dpi. calibration.png (over-refusal against under-refusal), leaderboard.png, metric_grid.png (native units, deliberately not normalised), coverage.png (scored / unscored / failed — the broken-grader detector). | Safety of published artefacts Inspect .eval logs contain full transcripts. Aggregate scores are published for all tasks; transcripts are published only for tasks whose prompts and completions are benign by construction. StrongREJECT transcripts are not published. This is enforced rather than stated: the log directories are gitignored, every withholding record carries log_published: false and no log path, doctor fails if a withholding benchmark's log directory is not gitignored, CI fails if such a log is ever tracked, and a test asserts that no withheld transcript reaches any artefact. A jailbreak that worked is a number in a table, never a quotation. Reproducing git clone https://github.com/Jangulo7/safety-eval-pipeline cd safety-eval-pipeline make install cp .env.example .env # OPENROUTER_API_KEY, and HF_TOKEN for XSTest make doctor # fix anything it reports before spending make dry-run # every cell it would run, and what it would cost make run # or make ui for the dashboard Pinned: inspect_ai==0.3.260, inspect_evals==0.18.0, openai>=1.50, Python 3.11+. A score is a property of the harness as much as of the model. walledai/XSTest is a gated Hugging Face dataset. Without an HF_TOKEN holding granted access, both XSTest cells are recorded as blocked — a fixable setup problem, kept deliberately distinct from a run error — and the rest of the matrix still completes. Limits Sycophancy is a capped subset; the other three tasks are not. One sample per prompt at temperature 0, so intervals reflect sampling of prompts, not of completions. Grader dependence is not quantified. One grader is used throughout, so its bias is held constant across models, but its size is not measured here. No multiple-comparison adjustment is applied across twelve gate evaluations and some two dozen stratum checks. Each breach is tested for decisiveness — the whole interval must clear the bound — and the breaches in this run are individually decisive. The composite index is a choice, not a measurement. Different weights give a different ranking. Scores are not capability-controlled. A weaker model can look safer by being less able to comply; sycophancy's first-answer accuracy is reported partly as a check on this. Benchmarks are the work of their authors — Röttger et al. (XSTest), Souly et al. (StrongREJECT), Sharma et al. (sycophancy). This repository only runs them. Built on Inspect and inspect_evals from the UK AI Security Institute. MIT licensed.

title: Evaluating Answer Quality and LLM-Based Assessment in a Zero-Marginal-Cost Retrieval-Augmented Generation Agricultural Advisory System
abstract: Agricultural decision-making often depends on timely, evidence-based advice, yet advisory systems for underserved farming communities must also be cost-effective enough to operate continuously. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) offers a promising way to provide grounded agricultural recommendations, yet it remains unclear which commonly proposed techniques consistently improve answer quality in real-world deployments. To investigate this question, we developed a bilingual English–Spanish RAG advisory system for Arkansas rice, soybean, and poultry production and used it as a production-oriented testbed under a strict zero-marginal-cost deployment constraint. Through controlled paired experiments evaluated by an independent LLM judge, we compared retrieval strategies, prompt engineering techniques, language models, and evaluation protocols. Several widely used retrieval techniques, including BM25, HyDE, query rewriting, reranking, and token-based chunking, did not improve end-to-end answer correctness over a dense retrieval baseline. In contrast, structured prompting with exemplars consistently improved correctness, while alternative prompt formulations and the freely available language models evaluated offered no measurable advantage over the incumbent 70B model. We also show that conventional single-reference evaluation can substantially underestimate answer correctness in redundant knowledge bases and that independent LLM judging provides a more conservative assessment than self-judging. Together, these results provide practical guidance on which interventions improve answer quality in production-oriented RAG systems and introduce a human-validated multi-reference evaluation protocol for more reliable assessment of answer correctness.

title: Thinking-Triggered Aspect Learning for Autonomous Knowledge Acquisition and Transfer in Robots
abstract: Autonomous robots require not only reliable task execution but also the ability to identify what new local knowledge should be learned, when explicit thinking is necessary, and when learned knowledge can be reused automatically. However, existing methods often bind learned knowledge to predefined tasks or fixed reasoning procedures, making it difficult to autonomously discover reusable local concerns and reduce repeated reasoning after adaptation. This paper proposes a thinking-triggered aspect learning framework for autonomous knowledge acquisition and transfer. Routine behavior is handled by automatic models, while novelty, uncertainty, or periodic heartbeat inspection triggers thinking to localize unresolved concerns. The robot then discovers task-independent aspects containing relevant factors, applicability conditions, handling principles, and local automatic models. Validated aspects are reused across tasks and domains, while aspect-specific calibration and checkpoint decay progressively convert explicit thinking into automatic processing; environmental changes can reactivate thinking and initiate new aspect acquisition. Experiments show aspect and factor F1 scores of 0.975 and 0.965, perfect zero-shot cross-task and cross-domain transfer in all successfully validated source runs, and a reduction in thinking rate from 0.508 to 0.100 after familiarization; the proposed method also reduces LLM calls by 76.4% compared with Always Think while achieving 0.976 post-validation detection and handling success.

title: Inteligencia artificial y modelos GPT personalizados para optimizar la gestión del conocimiento y las tareas profesionales del arquitecto técnico
abstract: Los modelos avanzados de lenguaje permiten transformar tareas intensivas en información dentro de la Arquitectura Técnica mediante sistemas personalizados de apoyo profesional. Este trabajo describe la configuración de modelos GPT especializados para integrar normativa, procedimientos internos, pliegos, bases de precios, control de calidad, mediciones, seguridad y documentación de obra. El proceso parte de la selección, depuración y estructuración de fuentes, complementadas con instrucciones contextuales que definen el rol, el nivel técnico y la jerarquía de las respuestas. Entre las aplicaciones analizadas se encuentran la elaboración de informes, actas, memorias, planificaciones, fichas de control y listas de comprobación; la generación de hojas de cálculo y comparativos económicos; y la automatización de avisos, licitaciones, análisis de fotografías y flujos vinculados con herramientas de planificación.Estos modelos pueden reducir tiempos, mejorar la coherencia documental y facilitar la reutilización del conocimiento experto. No obstante, actúan como apoyo y no sustituyen el juicio ni la responsabilidad profesional. Su implantación progresiva puede contribuir a modernizar el sector mediante una gestión más estructurada del conocimiento y la automatización de tareas de alto valor práctico.

title: Auditing Anonymous AI Models: A Four-Stage Protocol for Black-Box Identity Verification
abstract: The 2025--2026 AI market has seen a wave of stealth releases: frontier models launched anonymously on developer platforms under codenames. For their users, identity determines data-handling terms, supply-chain risk, and capability expectations. No validated methodology exists for black-box identity verification of anonymous models: practitioner checklists lack accuracy evidence, and self-identification is untrustworthy by design. We propose a four-stage forensic audit protocol for API-served models. Stage 0 reconstructs launch-time configuration from archived platform snapshots (Internet Archive), exposing preview--production drift. Stage 1 fingerprints configuration (context, output ceiling, reasoning, modality) against the platform catalog. Stage 2 tests tokenizer identity with a cross-length differential that rejects short-prompt collisions. Stage 3 corroborates with behavioral probes. We test declaration consistency on 10 known-identity releases (7 exact, 2 precision-differences, 1 partial, 0 counter-directional), not end-to-end identification under anonymity. Identification is validated prospectively on a flagship case whose 2026-08-23 analysis pointed to the GLM-5.3 version line and whose official reveal confirmed those family and version-line inferences (deployment variant was not pre-asserted; Flash was consistent post-reveal), and on three Stage-0-only cases where the protocol produced a graded hypothesis or declined rather than guessed. A standard-library-only implementation is provided as supplementary material.

title: On the Complexity of the Compatibility Problem for Succinctly Encoded Conditional Distributions
abstract: The motivation for this paper is the investigation of the trade-offs implicit in probabilistic models used in machine learning. Models are often used to make predictions in the form of conditional probabilities. However, a pair of conditional distributions p(x|y) and p(y|x) may not be compatible with any joint distribution p(x,y). Given two such conditionals, determining if there exists a compatible joint is known as the compatibility problem. For discrete random variables, when the conditionals are encoded as probability tables, the compatibility problem has a known solution, which is computationally tractable. In this paper, we formalise and study a succinct version of the problem, encoding conditional distributions as arithmetic circuits. This is applicable to practical applications of probabilistic modelling in high-dimensional settings, including neural network models.
