title: MELON: A Large-Scale Dataset for Multi-Event Text-to-Long-Video Retrieval
abstract: Existing text-video retrieval datasets primarily consist of short-form clips containing a single dominant event. While suitable for measuring basic vision-language alignment, they are limited in capturing real-world retrieval scenarios, where long-form videos naturally contain multiple semantically distinct events and a single text query may correspond to several non-contiguous temporal segments. To bridge this gap, we introduce MELON, the first large-scale dataset designed to extend text-video retrieval to long-form videos featuring complex, multi-event structures. MELON explicitly annotates multiple event intervals per video along with their corresponding textual descriptions, enabling both training and evaluation of multi-event understanding in long, untrimmed videos. In addition, we propose a multi-event aware loss that encourages models to differentiate between full-event and partial-event matches, yielding substantial improvements in retrieval accuracy. Together, the MELON dataset and our proposed loss establish a robust foundation for expanding text-to-video retrieval to complex long-form scenarios and provide a more realistic evaluation setting for future research in the field.

title: Distributed Implicit Harm: A Compositional Safety Blind Spot in MLLM-Based Video Moderation
abstract: Despite their growing use in video moderation, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) exhibit a compositional safety blind spot: videos composed of seemingly benign components can convey harmful meaning when interpreted as a whole. We refer to this phenomenon as Distributed Implicit Harm (DIH), where harm arises from relations among components distributed along a decomposition axis of the video, rather than from any single explicit cue. Among many possible axes, we study two representative cases: temporally distributed harm across visual segments (DIH-T) and cross-modal harm between audio and visual streams (DIH-M). Studying and mitigating DIH at scale requires data that is difficult to collect: such videos lack compositional harm annotations, evade retrieval based on local visual cues, keywords, or single-modality signals, and are consequently absent from existing safety datasets. To bridge this gap, we develop a multi-agent synthesis framework that composes individually benign components into harmful scenarios and generates diverse DIH videos with explicit reasoning annotations, yielding a dataset of over 9,000 videos spanning visual-only and audio-visual settings. Benchmarking over 30 MLLMs spanning frontier proprietary models and leading open-source systems reveals substantial and consistent deficits in detecting both DIH-T and DIH-M. Notably, this failure persists even among the strongest frontier models: they often correctly assess individual components in isolation but fail to recognize the harmful meaning that emerges from their composition. We further evaluate these models on a manually collected set of real-world DIH videos from social media and observe the same failure mode, highlighting DIH as a practical and underexplored challenge for video moderation.

title: TDDM-Melatt: A Decoupled Memory and Diffusion Framework for Generalizable Encrypted Traffic Classification
abstract: The widespread adoption of encrypted traffic poses severe challenges to current security situational awareness systems based on network traffic monitoring. In existing dataset-driven training and testing studies, limitations such as shortcut learning induced by spurious feature correlations and sample imbalance caused by the long-tail distribution of real-world traffic result in weak generalization of traffic identification performance to real-world network traffic. To address these limitations, we propose TDDM-Melatt, a disentangled memory-based traffic classification framework with diffusion-based data augmentation. First, we design Melatt, a memory-decoupled traffic representation model, which employs Competitive Gating Long Short-Term Memory (CG-LSTM) to construct the encoder and decoder. We design a spurious-correlation-free pre-training and inference paradigm, employing strict topology anonymization and a frozen pre-trained encoder strategy to cut off the model's learning pathways for spurious features. During inference, classification is performed efficiently by a downstream classifier on the frozen representations. Second, we propose a Traffic Denoising Diffusion Model (TDDM) tailored to the characteristics of traffic data. Extensive experiments are conducted on 4 representative public benchmark datasets. Under strict flow-level splitting and anonymization, TDDM-Melatt outperforms 6 basic classification models and 6 SOTA representation learning models. The proposed method provides a new and effective technical pathway for encrypted traffic classification in real-world network environments.

title: What It Costs to Compose, Rebuild, and Correct Precomputed Memory
abstract: Language models can answer from precomputed memory, a model's saved reading of a body of material, reused across requests instead of read again at each. This paper maps where that practice preserves correctness and the conditions under which it fails. Across experiments on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct using both saved key-value caches and trained compressions of them, precomputed memory degrades when assembled from separately prepared parts, stays current only through rebuilds costing a large fraction of full preparation in our measurements, and ignores corrections served beside it conditional on phrasing. If precomputed memories can be served alongside one another, be cost-efficiently rebuilt, and be superseded by new information arriving in real-time, they can serve as a way to avoid re-feeding context to a model over repeated queries. The implication of our results for a deployed system that deals with a variety of queries is that precomputed memories are best rebuilt on the cadence at which new information changes what the memory was originally computed from. Both warm-rebuilding trained compressions of key-value caches and serving specifically-phrased updates beside a memory, as pasted text or injected cache state, show particular promise for keeping precomputed memories current, the latter as an interim measure between rebuilds, and we measure the cost and name the remaining questions associated with each.

title: PAVE: Predictive Alignment and Value-Guided Evolution for World-Action Policies
abstract: Direct vision-language-action policies generate continuous robot actions efficiently, but standard behavior cloning leaves two complementary gaps: their representations are not explicitly required to describe how the scene evolves over multiple time scales, and deployment trajectories of unequal quality are often reused without separating useful dynamics from undesirable behavior. We introduce \method, a direct world-action policy that combines outcome-agnostic predictive learning with outcome-aware policy improvement. \method first retains a local fixed-offset JEPA objective and adds trajectory-relative multi-horizon transition alignment at 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% of the remaining episode. These training-only targets require the current policy representation to preserve both local physical changes and longer-range task progress, without supplying explicit future tokens to the action head. \method then trains an independent distributional value critic on cumulative deployment trajectories, computes action-chunk-aligned $N$-step advantages, and converts them into positive, negative, or null text conditions for a flow-matching actor. Thus, every valid trajectory can teach what physically happened, while the actor is deployed only under the condition associated with relatively better actions. The multi-horizon predictor and critic are removed from online execution, preserving direct action generation from the current observation, language instruction, and proprioception. \redclaim{Across the three simulation benchmarks, \method achieves the strongest overall performance while preserving the direct actor's online execution path.}

The multi-horizon predictor and critic are removed from online execution, preserving direct action generation from the current observation, language instruction, and proprioception. \redclaim{Across the three simulation benchmarks, \method achieves the strongest overall performance while preserving the direct actor's online execution path.}

title: Diffusion-Based Refinement for Kilometer-Scale Probabilistic Precipitation Nowcasting
abstract: Localized extreme precipitation is a major trigger of urban flash floods and landslides, yet producing nowcasts that combine fine spatial detail with probabilistic uncertainty remains challenging. Here we introduce exPreCast-ENS, a conditional residual diffusion framework that transforms the deterministic 4 km radar nowcaster exPreCast into a 1 km probabilistic ensemble while correcting systematic forecast errors. Conditioning on both the forecast and preceding radar observations lets the ensemble-mean correct the baseline rather than perturb it, while members represent unresolved fine-scale variability. Over the Korean Peninsula, skill improves with ensemble size. In two high-impact events in 2023, a 30-member ensemble recovers 38-47% of heavy-rain pixels missed by exPreCast while retaining approximately 95% of its correct detections and alarming on under 1% of the pixels it correctly left clear. The method generates a 1-h forecast in 3.4 s on a single GPU and yields consistent improvements on the French regional MeteoNet radar dataset.

title: IDENTIFIKASI SENTIMEN PENGGUNA APLIKASI JKN BERBASIS TERM FREQUENCY-DOCUMENT FREQUENCY DAN SUPPORT VECTOR MACHINE
abstract: Abstract: User reviews of the Jaminan Kesehatan Nasional (JKN) mobile application on app distribution platforms continue to increase in line with the growing use of digital health services in Indonesia. These reviews contain sentiments related to the application, yet they have not been systematically analyzed to reveal user perception and satisfaction toward the JKN application. This study aims to analyze sentiment in JKN application reviews by employing the Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) method combined with the Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm. The review data processing stage began with preprocessing, comprising cleaning, case folding, tokenization, stopword removal, and stemming, followed by weighting using TF-IDF to transform textual data into numerical data in accordance with word occurrence frequency. The weighting results then served as input for the SVM algorithm to construct a separating hyperplane between classes, thereby classifying reviews into positive or negative categories. The research dataset consisted of 10,000 JKN application user reviews obtained through scraping from the Google Play Store platform. The testing results showed an accuracy of 99.83%, precision of 99.92%, recall of 99.83%, and an F1-score of 99.87%. These results demonstrate that the combination of TF-IDF and SVM can produce highly accurate sentiment classification of JKN application user reviews. User perception and satisfaction obtained from this sentiment identification serve as an evaluative basis for JKN application administrators to encourage improvements in the quality of digital health services in Indonesia. Keyword: Sentiment Analysis, TF-IDF, JKN, Support Vector Machine, User Reviews. Abstrak: Ulasan pengguna aplikasi Jaminan Kesehatan Nasional (JKN) pada platform distribusi aplikasi terus bertambah seiring meningkatnya penggunaan layanan kesehatan digital di Indonesia. Ulasan tersebut memuat sentimen terkait kualitas layanan, kemudahan penggunaan, dan kinerja fitur, namun belum dianalisis secara sistematis untuk mengetahui persepsi dan kepuasan pengguna terhadap aplikasi JKN. Sentimen dalam ulasan pengguna aplikasi JKN dianalisis menggunakan metode Term Frequency Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) dan Support Vector Machine (SVM) sebagai tujuan dari penelitian ini. Tahapan untuk mengolah data ulasan pada penelitian ini merupakan preprocessing (cleaning, case folding, tokenization, stopword removal, dan stemming), disusul pembobotan memakai TF-IDF agar data teks bertransformasi menjadi data numerik selaras dengan frekuensi kemunculan kata. Hasil pembobotan menjadi input bagi algoritma SVM untuk membentuk hyperplane pemisah antar kelas, sehingga ulasan diklasifikasikan ke dalam kategori positif atau negatif. Dataset penelitian berjumlah 10.000 ulasan pengguna aplikasi JKN yang diperoleh melalui scraping dari platform Google Play Store. Hasil pengujian dari penelitian yaitu akurasi sebesar 99,83%, presisi 99,92%, recall 99,83%, dan F1-score 99,87%. Hasil dari pengujian tersebut membuktikan kombinasi TF-IDF dan SVM dapat menghasilkan klasifikasi sentimen ulasan pengguna aplikasi JKN dengan ketepatan tinggi. Gambaran mengenai persepsi dan kepuasan pengguna diperoleh dari hasil identifikasi sentimen ini untuk bahan evaluasi bagi pengelola aplikasi JKN guna mendorong peningkatan kualitas layanan kesehatan digital di Indonesia. Kata kunci: Analisis Sentimen, TF-IDF, JKN, Support Vector Machine, Ulasan Pengguna.

title: Dimension Space Quantum Information Encryption
abstract: This paper investigates the concept of Dimension Space Quantum Information Encryption (DSQIE), a novel cryptographic scheme predicated on the manipulation of quantum entanglement and key distribution. We propose a method leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to establish a high-level security guarantee for data transmission. The core of this approach is the utilization of quantum key distribution (QKD) combined with the inherent security of entanglement, designed to mitigate vulnerabilities inherent in classical encryption. This paper outlines the theoretical underpinnings of DSQIE, detailing its mechanism, security considerations, and potential applications within the context of modern cybersecurity. The research explores the feasibility of utilizing entanglement to create unbreakable encryption keys, offering a fundamentally different approach to data protection.

title: Quantum Machine Learning Geometric Optimization
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) offers a paradigm shift in computational capabilities, potentially unlocking solutions to complex problems previously intractable with classical algorithms. Geometric optimization, a core challenge in various fields, presents a particularly demanding scenario. This paper investigates the application of quantum algorithms, specifically leveraging quantum entanglement and superposition, to address geometric optimization problems. We propose a novel QML framework centered on the manipulation of geometric representations using quantum states, aiming to significantly enhance the efficiency and accuracy of solutions compared to classical methods. The core mechanism involves encoding geometric constraints and objective functions into quantum states, facilitating distributed and entangled operations for efficient exploration of the solution space. This research explores the potential of this approach to tackle problems ranging from shape optimization and surface reconstruction to logistics and resource allocation. We present a preliminary implementation of a QML-based optimization algorithm with a focus on demonstrating its potential for solving certain geometric optimization scenarios. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential challenges.

title: Blockchain-Based Distributed Secure Multi-Party Computation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for secure multi-party computation (SMPC) utilizing blockchain technology. The core idea is to establish a trusted environment for computation among multiple parties without revealing their private data. We leverage zero-knowledge proofs (ZKP) and homomorphic encryption to enable computations while maintaining data confidentiality. The blockchain infrastructure provides transparency and auditability throughout the entire process. This approach addresses the inherent trust issues associated with traditional SMPC solutions that rely on a central trusted third party. The system guarantees that each party's input remains private, and the final result of the computation is verifiable. This design offers a more decentralized and secure alternative for sensitive data processing tasks. The system utilizes cryptographic primitives to ensure the integrity and privacy of the computations. The underlying architecture provides a robust mechanism for managing access control and verifying the validity of the computation results. This paper outlines the system architecture, key components, and the mathematical foundations that underpin its security and functionality. ---

title: Self-Referential Graph Neural Networks for Recursive Knowledge Acquisition
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to knowledge acquisition in Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) using a self-referential architecture. The core idea is to create a GNN that can recursively evaluate and refine its own representations through the incorporation of feedback loops. This is achieved by introducing a "meta-layer" within the GNN architecture. This meta-layer analyzes the output of the primary GNN layer and adjusts the parameters of the primary layer to enhance predictive performance and, crucially, improve the knowledge acquisition process. The resulting self-referential GNN demonstrates the potential for recursive learning, offering a pathway to more robust and adaptable GNN models. We detail the architecture, the feedback mechanism, and the theoretical underpinnings of this approach. The primary goal is to demonstrate a method for GNNs to dynamically improve their understanding of graph data through internal assessment and adjustment.

title: Corrections to Geometric Field Geometry – A Quantum Entanglement-Based Validation Method
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to geometric field geometry validation utilizing quantum entanglement. The core claim is to develop a method capable of detecting geometric errors, particularly within high-dimensional geometric spaces, offering a more precise validation compared to conventional methods. This investigation leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to encode geometric information and implement instantaneous verification, effectively circumventing the limitations of classical geometric validation. The paper details the mechanism, including quantum state encoding and entanglement network verification, and explores its potential for achieving robust and accurate geometric error detection.

title: 基于自适应的量子机器学习的拓扑信息提取
abstract: This paper explores the application of a novel quantum machine learning framework, termed "Adaptive Quantum Machine Learning" (AQML), for the extraction of crucial topological information from complex datasets. Traditional data analysis and feature extraction methods often rely on manual intervention, limiting efficiency and potentially introducing human bias. AQML leverages quantum computing's inherent parallelism to automatically identify and isolate key topological features within datasets, dramatically enhancing the speed and accuracy of analysis. We present a detailed implementation of the AQML algorithm, outlining its architecture, computational methodology, and validation results. This approach promises to revolutionize data analysis by automating the extraction of critical topological properties, enabling more efficient and insightful data exploration. This work is motivated by the need for more robust and adaptable methods in the analysis of complex, high-dimensional datasets, particularly in fields such as materials science, biology, and network analysis.

title: 基于图的自适应神经网络的量子机器学习
abstract: This paper explores the integration of graph neural networks (GNNs) with quantum machine learning (QML) to address the challenges of complex data analysis. We propose a novel framework that utilizes a graph-structured neural network as the primary input for a quantum computation, enabling rapid pattern discovery and automated parameter adjustment. The core mechanism centers on leveraging quantum parallelism to accelerate the learning process within the GNN architecture. The paper details the implementation of the framework, discusses its performance compared to classical methods, and outlines potential applications across diverse data types. We demonstrate that this hybrid approach offers a significant advantage in learning and predicting intricate relationships within complex graph structures. This work represents a step towards a paradigm shift in data analysis, combining the strengths of both graph theory and quantum computation.

title: Variable-Adaptive Quantum Algorithms
abstract: This paper introduces a novel variable-adaptive quantum algorithm designed to enhance the efficiency and precision of quantum computations by dynamically adjusting quantum operations based on input data variations. Traditional quantum algorithms often require pre-computation, and this approach aims to mitigate this by minimizing computational overhead through real-time operational adjustments. The core mechanism involves a sophisticated feedback loop that continuously monitors input data and adjusts quantum operations to optimize the algorithm's performance. The study explores the potential benefits of this dynamic approach in various quantum applications.

abstract: Quantum networks offer the potential for unparalleled secure communication and distributed quantum computing, but the inherent complexity of quantum systems necessitates efficient and robust optimization techniques. This paper introduces a novel quantum network topology optimization algorithm based on a self-adaptive topology structure, leveraging quantum network properties for automated adjustments. We propose a framework that dynamically adjusts network parameters to enhance quantum information transmission and processing, demonstrating improved performance compared to existing methods. The core mechanism centers around a dynamically evolving topology, allowing for optimized quantum states. This approach minimizes errors and maximizes fidelity in quantum information transfer and processing.

title: 基于多模态信息融合的自适应强化学习
abstract: This paper investigates the application of multimodal information fusion within the framework of adaptive reinforcement learning. The core claim is that integrating diverse input modalities, such as images, text, and audio, into the decision-making process of reinforcement learning agents significantly enhances their adaptive learning capabilities. The proposed mechanism leverages multimodal information representation learning to map different modalities into a common vector space. These vectors then serve as input to the reinforcement learning algorithm, leading to improved learning efficiency and generalization performance. The novelty of this research lies in the nascent stage of algorithm design and training methodologies for multimodal reinforcement learning. This work explores a framework for addressing this challenge, outlining key considerations and potential approaches. We define the problem as maximizing cumulative reward in an environment where the agent receives sensory input from multiple modalities. The agent learns a policy that maps states (represented as multimodal feature vectors) to actions, aiming to achieve the highest possible reward. We introduce a novel adaptive weighting scheme for combining multimodal features, allowing the agent to dynamically adjust its reliance on each modality based on its relevance to the current situation. This weighting is learned through a meta-reinforcement learning process. Furthermore, we explore the use of attention mechanisms to focus on the most salient features within each modality, further improving the agent's ability to extract relevant information. The ultimate goal is to create a robust and adaptable reinforcement learning agent capable of effectively utilizing diverse sensory inputs for optimal decision-making.

title: Non-Euclidean Neural Network Architecture – Dynamic Layer Arrangement
abstract: This paper investigates a novel neural network architecture – the Dynamic Layer Arrangement (DLA) model – that dynamically adjusts the arrangement of layers based on the data's distribution. Traditional neural networks rely on fixed layer configurations, limiting their ability to effectively capture complex data patterns. The DLA model leverages non-Euclidean geometric principles to optimize information flow and feature aggregation, resulting in improved performance across various datasets. We introduce a novel metric to quantify data distribution and utilize this metric to dynamically re-arrange layers, fostering a more adaptable and efficient network structure. This research demonstrates the potential of this approach to overcome the limitations of conventional architectures and achieve superior results in a range of tasks.

title: Title: Non-Local Constraint Optimization for Quantum Circuits (NLOCQ)
abstract: Quantum circuit design presents a significant challenge due to the inherent complexity of optimizing numerous parameters across multiple qubits. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with the computational demands of fully solving the optimization problem, particularly when dealing with large quantum systems. This paper introduces Non-Local Constraint Optimization for Quantum Circuits (NLOCQ), a novel approach that leverages quantum entanglement to enable efficient and scalable optimization of quantum circuit parameters without explicitly solving the full optimization problem. NLOCQ utilizes a distributed search strategy, exploiting quantum entanglement to create a 'distributed' optimization process, thereby reducing computational burden and enabling exploration of a significantly larger search space. We demonstrate the effectiveness of NLOCQ through a series of simulations, showcasing its ability to efficiently optimize quantum circuits and achieve optimal performance compared to classical methods under specific benchmark scenarios. The core mechanism centers around creating entangled states to represent potential solutions, facilitating rapid exploration and identification of optimal parameter configurations. This work represents a significant advancement in quantum circuit optimization, offering a promising pathway to more efficient and practical quantum design.

abstract: This paper presents a novel theoretical framework, Dynamic Holographic Resonance (DHR), exploring the potential of holographic principles to accelerate the development of highly efficient quantum computation. We propose a model wherein the holographic principle is treated as a continuously evolving, dynamic field, capable of optimizing quantum circuit designs and algorithms through iterative refinement. We investigate the interplay between the holographic principle, circuit optimization, and the inherent properties of quantum entanglement, suggesting a pathway toward achieving exponential speedups in quantum computations. This work contributes to a deeper understanding of the fundamental role of holographic data in guiding the design of quantum systems.

We propose a model wherein the holographic principle is treated as a continuously evolving, dynamic field, capable of optimizing quantum circuit designs and algorithms through iterative refinement. The core mechanism leverages this dynamic field to identify and exploit subtle correlations inherent in quantum systems, ultimately aiming to surpass the limitations of current quantum computing approaches. We investigate the interplay between the holographic principle, circuit optimization, and the inherent properties of quantum entanglement, suggesting a pathway toward achieving exponential speedups in quantum computations. This work contributes to a deeper understanding of the fundamental role of holographic data in guiding the design of quantum systems.

title: An Approach to Program Optimization Using Simulated Annealing
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to program optimization leveraging the Simulated Annealing (SA) algorithm. The core idea is to model program code as an optimization problem, where the goal is to find the most efficient and performant version. SA's ability to escape local optima is effectively utilized to explore the vast solution space of possible code modifications. This method aims to improve program performance and efficiency by iteratively refining the code through simulated thermal fluctuations. The presented approach offers a flexible and potentially powerful technique for program optimization, particularly for complex programs where traditional optimization methods may struggle. The paper details the methodology, including code representation, the SA algorithm implementation, and a discussion on key parameters influencing the optimization process. ---

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Geometric Modeling - Holographic Morphing
abstract: Quantum-enhanced geometric modeling seeks to leverage the principles of quantum mechanics and holographic geometry to create complex, self-morphing shapes. This paper explores a novel approach utilizing a 'Quantum Morphing Field' – a system designed to automatically analyze an object and generate a morphing field, facilitating the creation of intricate geometric forms. The core claim is to develop a method for modeling geometric objects using quantum mechanics and holographic principles, enabling the automatic creation of complex, self-morphing shapes. This work focuses on the implementation of a 'Quantum Morphing Field' as the central mechanism, demonstrating its potential for generating novel geometric transformations.

title: Quantum Information in Topological Landscapes
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum information to the modeling of topological landscapes, leveraging quantum entanglement and quantum algorithms to achieve efficient modeling and processing of topological properties. We investigate the potential of utilizing quantum mechanics to enhance the accuracy and computational efficiency of topological structure analysis. The core mechanism involves the implementation of quantum-enhanced algorithms and the application of quantum principles to optimize topological representations. This research presents a novel approach to tackling challenges in topological data analysis and representation. The study focuses on the interplay between quantum entanglement, quantum algorithms, and topological landscape modeling, aiming to provide a deeper understanding of their potential impact.

title: Bergmans's Collared Fruit Bat: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Bergmans's Collared Fruit Bat" (BCFB), inspired by the foraging behavior of *Pteropus* bats, specifically Bergmann's Collared Fruit Bats. These bats exhibit a complex and efficient foraging strategy, utilizing echo location and dynamic adjustments to their flight paths to maximize food acquisition. BCFB leverages these observed behaviors to create a search algorithm designed for optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates key elements of bat foraging, including a position update mechanism based on echo location (distance to the best solution), a social influence component mimicking group foraging, and a dynamic flight strategy incorporating randomness and exploration. The performance of BCFB is evaluated through a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential advantages over existing metaheuristic techniques. The algorithm's design aims to balance exploration and exploitation, leading to robust and efficient solution convergence. The core of the algorithm lies in a modified particle representation, where particles are not merely positions but also represent the 'echo' – a measure of distance to the current best solution – facilitating informed decision-making. The paper concludes by discussing potential extensions and future research directions.

title: 基于自适应的量子势场优化
abstract: The pursuit of accurate and reliable quantum computation necessitates sophisticated control over quantum systems. Traditional approaches often rely on static optimization strategies, limiting the system's ability to dynamically adapt to changing conditions. This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive quantum potential field optimization method, leveraging dynamic adjustment of the quantum potential to achieve precise quantum control and significantly enhance the precision of quantum calculations. The core mechanism centers around an adaptive algorithm that continuously refines the quantum potential based on the system's state, providing a robust and automated approach to quantum control. We present a rigorous theoretical analysis and initial experimental validation demonstrating the superior performance of this method over established static optimization techniques. The focus is on enhancing the accuracy and controllability of quantum systems, opening doors to more complex and impactful quantum computations.

title: Behzad's Brush-tailed Mouse: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Petauroides brachyurus*
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Behzad's Brush-tailed Mouse (BBTM), inspired by the foraging strategies of *Petauroides brachyurus*, commonly known as the Brush-tailed Rock-wallaby. Rock-wallabies are renowned for their efficient and adaptable foraging behavior, particularly their ability to navigate complex environments and exploit patchy resources. BBTM leverages these observed characteristics through a combination of adaptive parameter control, a novel exploration strategy based on simulated movement patterns, and a refined exploitation mechanism focused on gradient estimation. The algorithm's core innovation lies in dynamically adjusting parameters based on the observed resource density and the agent's movement history, mimicking the rock-wallaby's response to environmental changes. Performance evaluations on a range of benchmark optimization problems demonstrate that BBTM exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, including Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). The algorithm's adaptability and ability to handle complex landscapes are highlighted, suggesting potential applications in diverse fields such as engineering design, financial modeling, and machine learning.

title: 基于动态概率模型的自适应机器学习
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic probability model-based self-adaptive machine learning framework. Traditional machine learning relies on static models, while this framework dynamically adjusts model parameters based on the input data's probability distribution, enabling precise data distribution modeling. The core mechanism involves simulating data distributions and automatically tuning model parameters to enhance adaptability. This approach offers a significant improvement in handling evolving data patterns compared to traditional methods. We present a theoretical analysis demonstrating the framework's effectiveness and provide a practical implementation demonstrating its capabilities.

title: Dynamic Quantum Algorithm Topology Analysis
abstract: This paper explores the potential of dynamic quantum algorithms to adapt to input data's topological structure, leading to enhanced computational efficiency and precision. We propose a novel algorithm that dynamically adjusts quantum algorithm parameters based on the input, optimizing the algorithm's performance. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that continuously refines the quantum state to achieve optimal results. This approach contrasts sharply with traditional quantum algorithms, which typically rely on pre-defined parameters, offering a significant advancement in adaptability and control. The study delves into the theoretical underpinnings of this dynamic adjustment, examining its impact on algorithm convergence and accuracy. We provide a detailed analysis of the algorithm's design, showcasing its potential for solving complex problems with improved computational throughput.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Measurement Protocol
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers a unique pathway toward secure and efficient quantum information transfer. This paper explores the design and implementation of a novel quantum entanglement-based measurement protocol, termed the "Quantum Entanglement-Based Measurement Protocol" (QEBMP), aimed at achieving high accuracy and low latency in quantum information transmission. The core of the protocol hinges on leveraging entanglement to detect minuscule changes in quantum states, offering a distinct advantage over classical communication methods. We detail the protocol's architecture, highlighting the critical role of entanglement-induced correlations in enabling precise measurement and detection. The research focuses on establishing a robust and efficient mechanism for quantifying and interpreting entanglement fluctuations, contributing to the advancement of quantum technologies.

title: Information Theory-Based Robustness Analysis of Deep Neural Networks
abstract: Deep neural networks have achieved remarkable success in various domains, but their vulnerability to adversarial attacks poses a significant challenge. This work presents a novel approach to evaluating the robustness of deep neural networks using information-theoretic principles. Specifically, we leverage concepts of mutual information and entropy to quantify the network's sensitivity to input perturbations. Our analysis demonstrates that the information flow within the network is a crucial determinant of its robustness. By identifying areas of high information flow vulnerability, we provide insights for designing more resilient architectures and training strategies. The core contribution is a rigorous framework for assessing neural network robustness based on quantifiable information-theoretic measures, offering a new perspective on adversarial vulnerability and potential mitigation techniques.

title: Continuous Time Reinforcement Learning with Temporal Logic
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to reinforcement learning (RL) that extends its applicability to continuous time environments. Traditional RL methods often rely on discrete time steps, which can be inadequate for modeling systems where temporal relationships and constraints are crucial. We propose a framework that leverages continuous-time Markov decision processes (CTMDPs) and temporal logic to define complex objectives. The core idea is to translate the RL problem into a CTMDP, where reward functions and constraints are explicitly specified using temporal logic. This enables the learning of policies that not only maximize reward but also adhere to stringent temporal specifications, such as deadlines or safety requirements. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical framework and outline its potential applications in areas such as robotics, control systems, and resource management. The key contribution lies in providing a rigorous methodology for integrating temporal reasoning into the RL process, addressing a significant gap in current RL research. The proposed method offers a more expressive and adaptable solution for tackling complex, temporally-constrained control problems.

title: Title: Dynamically Constrained Tensor Networks for Deep Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for constructing tensor networks, specifically designed to improve the generalization performance of deep learning models. Traditional tensor network approaches often rely on static topology design, limiting the model's capacity to adapt to diverse data. We propose a dynamic constraint algorithm that iteratively adjusts network connections and weights based on observed performance during training. This approach mitigates the limitations of static topology, allowing for more robust and adaptable models. The core mechanism leverages a feedback loop that dynamically modifies the network, optimizing for both accuracy and generalization. This work addresses a critical challenge in deep learning: the lack of adaptability in current methods.

title: Assam Mole Shrew: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Xipolitoxodon*
abstract: This paper presents Assam Mole Shrew (AMS), a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Xipolitoxodon*, an extinct species of mole shrew endemic to Assam, India. *Xipolitoxodon* exhibits remarkable burrowing and foraging strategies, characterized by short, rapid bursts of movement followed by periods of stillness and exploratory sniffing. AMS leverages these behaviors to construct a novel search procedure. The algorithm utilizes a dynamic population of potential solutions, represented as vectors, and employs a "sniffing" mechanism to guide exploration. A "burst" component is introduced to simulate the animal's rapid movement, and a "pause" mechanism mimics its periods of stillness. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions. The core mathematical formulation of AMS is presented, focusing on the representation of solution vectors, the sniffing and burst parameters, and the update rules for population members. The results show that AMS performs competitively with established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA) in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. This research contributes a biologically inspired approach to optimization, demonstrating the potential of mimicking natural behaviors for algorithm design.

title: Quantum Entanglement and Non-Locality: A Novel Communication Protocol
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, presents a persistent challenge to our understanding of locality – the principle that an object can only be influenced by its immediate surroundings. This paper explores a novel non-local model based on quantum entanglement, aiming to mitigate the limitations of local realism and propose a new quantum communication protocol. Our core claim posits that by strategically manipulating entangled states, we can circumvent the inherent limitations of local interactions and establish secure communication channels. The proposed model leverages non-locality to enhance the robustness of quantum information transfer, offering a potential pathway towards practical quantum technologies.

title: ## Mimetic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by the Spotted Jaguar (MOA-SJ)
abstract: This paper introduces the Mimetic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by the Spotted Jaguar (MOA-SJ), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm designed to leverage the adaptive hunting strategies observed in the spotted jaguar (Panthera onca). The algorithm mimics the jaguar's ability to dynamically adjust its search strategy based on environmental changes, prey availability, and the perceived success of different hunting methods. MOA-SJ employs a population of 'hunters,' each possessing a unique 'hunting strategy' represented by a set of parameters. These parameters are continuously adjusted based on a 'mimicry coefficient' that reflects the perceived effectiveness of the current strategy, influenced by the performance of neighboring hunters and the overall objective function landscape. The algorithm incorporates a 'territory awareness' mechanism, analogous to the jaguar's territorial behavior, to avoid converging on local optima. This paper details the algorithm's formulation, including the key components of the hunting strategy, the mimicry coefficient calculation, and the territory awareness mechanism. The algorithm's potential applications and future research directions are also discussed.

title: ## Apeco Oldfield Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavioral Patterns of *Mylimus oldfieldi*
abstract: This paper proposes Apeco, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Mylimus oldfieldi* (Apeco Oldfield Mouse), a small rodent species known for its efficient exploration and exploitation of its environment. Apeco leverages the principles of trail following, resource assessment, and adaptive movement strategies observed in Apeco Oldfield Mice to develop a robust and effective optimization process. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach with a dynamically adjusted exploration-exploitation balance. Specifically, Apeco employs a 'Trail Strength' mechanism to represent the attractiveness of different solution regions, an 'Resource Density' function to estimate the potential of each solution, and an 'Adaptive Velocity' control scheme to regulate movement towards promising areas. The performance of Apeco is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capabilities against established metaheuristic algorithms. The key contributions of this work are the novel integration of these behavioral features into a metaheuristic framework and the empirical validation of its effectiveness. The algorithm's performance is analyzed through convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency.

title: 基于信息瓶颈理论的机器学习模型学习
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to machine learning model learning rooted in the Information Bottleneck (IB) theory. The core argument posits that the underlying learning process mirrors the phenomenon of information bottleneck, where a system is forced to discard irrelevant information while retaining only the most crucial features for a given task. We propose a learning algorithm designed to explicitly leverage this bottleneck effect, aiming to enhance learning efficiency and ultimately improve model performance. The algorithm utilizes a variational inference framework, incorporating an IB objective function to guide the representation learning process. The theoretical foundation of the approach is firmly grounded in IB theory, and we demonstrate, conceptually, how the constraints imposed by the IB objective function can lead to more robust and generalized representations. This work offers a new perspective on machine learning, suggesting that explicitly modeling information bottlenecks can be a powerful strategy for tackling complex learning challenges. The primary contribution lies in the design of a systematic method for incorporating IB principles into a machine learning algorithm, moving beyond simply applying IB as a regularization technique.

abstract: This paper explores the concept of multi-particle quantum entanglement and proposes a novel "Multi-Particle Information Encoding" technique leveraging the unique properties of entangled states. title: ## The Cicada-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (CIMO)
abstract: This paper introduces the Cicada-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (CIMO), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of cicadas. Cicadas, known for their remarkable ability to locate optimal food sources over vast distances, exhibit a strategy of probabilistic movement combined with a memory of previously visited locations. CIMO leverages these principles by employing a probabilistic movement strategy based on a dynamically adjusted probability distribution and a memory mechanism that stores the best solutions encountered during the search process. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, with each individual representing a potential solution. CIMO incorporates a "cicada phase" where individuals randomly explore the search space, combined with a "memory phase" where individuals are guided towards previously successful locations. The algorithm's parameters, including the exploration rate and memory influence, are adjusted adaptively to maintain a balance between exploration and exploitation. This paper outlines the theoretical framework of CIMO, its key components, and its potential applications in various optimization problems.

title: Andean Pygmy Rice Rat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Andean Pygmy Rice Rat Algorithm (APRRA), inspired by the foraging behavior of *Rattus norvegicus* pygmy rice rats inhabiting the Andean region. These rodents exhibit remarkable adaptation to scarce resources and challenging terrains, employing a sophisticated strategy of intermittent exploration and exploitation. The APRRA algorithm leverages this observed behavior to create a new optimization method. The core of the APRRA algorithm involves a dynamic population of agents, each representing a potential solution. These agents move through a search space, guided by a combination of attraction and repulsion forces, mimicking the rat's movement patterns in response to food sources and obstacles. A key component is the "nesting" behavior, where agents periodically consolidate their efforts around promising regions, similar to how rats construct and maintain nests for shelter and food storage. The algorithm incorporates a stochastic element based on the rat's unpredictable movement, enhancing exploration capabilities. Performance evaluations are presented on a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness and competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic techniques. The APRRA algorithm shows promising potential for solving complex optimization problems across diverse domains.

title: Quantum Privacy Computation Protocol Based on Quantum Coherence
abstract: This paper proposes a novel privacy computation protocol leveraging the principles of quantum coherence and decoherence. The core concept involves constructing a "black box" mechanism utilizing quantum states to interfere with the computation process, effectively masking the original data while guaranteeing the accuracy of the resulting output. Unlike existing approaches such as differential privacy and homomorphic encryption, this protocol harnesses quantum effects to provide enhanced privacy protection. We define the protocol as follows: Let *S1*, *S2*, ..., *SK* represent the shares of *K* parties. The protocol aims to compute a function *f* on these shares. The function *f* is implemented through a series of quantum gates, where each gate operates on the combined quantum state of all shares. Decoherence is induced by carefully designed interactions, specifically utilizing quantum measurement operators that introduce probabilistic errors. The probability of successfully executing the quantum computation is dependent on the strength and duration of the decoherence process. The resulting output, *O*, is obtained through a final quantum measurement. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of decoherence parameters, allowing for a tunable trade-off between privacy and computation accuracy. Further, we explore the mathematical foundations of this protocol, providing a formal description of the underlying quantum operations and the decoherence model. This work contributes a fundamental understanding of leveraging quantum decoherence for privacy-preserving computation and opens avenues for future research in quantum-enhanced security.

title: Adaptive Quantum Field Calibration via Dynamic Resonance Tuning
abstract: Quantum field calibration is a crucial aspect of quantum computing, ensuring precise control and stability. Traditional calibration methods are often static, failing to adapt to varying environments or device imperfections. This paper proposes a novel adaptive system for quantum field calibration, leveraging a dynamic resonance tuning algorithm. The system employs a continuous feedback loop to minimize errors by meticulously adjusting parameters based on real-time field response analysis. The core mechanism involves an algorithm that optimizes field resonance to maintain a desired accuracy level. This work addresses the limitations of current calibration techniques, offering a continuous, adaptive approach with the potential for significant improvements in quantum device performance.

title: Nonlinear Quantum Topology: Adaptive Mapping via Geometric Path Optimization
abstract: Quantum topology, a fascinating field, offers a unique perspective on the properties of space and time. This paper explores the application of non-linear quantum topology to adaptive mapping, specifically through the use of geometric path optimization. We introduce a novel algorithm that leverages the dynamic evolution of quantum topology represented by geometric paths to achieve precise parameter control and optimization. The core mechanism centers around constructing a quantum path representation, modeling its evolution, and employing optimization techniques tailored to these evolving paths. The proposed framework offers a fundamentally new approach to controlling quantum systems, promising advancements in quantum information processing and manipulation. This work provides a conceptual foundation for exploring complex quantum systems through a novel mapping strategy.

title: Title: Non-Linear Topological Phase Transitions in Machine Learning Models
abstract: This paper investigates the emergence of non-linear topological phase transitions within machine learning models, offering a novel perspective on model stability and robustness. Traditional approaches often focus on static model parameters, neglecting the dynamic nature of the system's structure. We propose a dynamic topology that allows for continuous changes in the model's framework, triggering new phases and ultimately leading to a qualitative shift in the learning process. Our analysis demonstrates the potential for these transitions to significantly impact model performance and generalization. We explore the underlying mechanisms driving this phenomenon through a combination of theoretical investigation and simulation. The findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the stability of machine learning models and have implications for the design of more resilient and adaptable AI systems.

abstract: Abstract: This paper explores the application of ultra-space geometry to quantum computation verification, aiming to provide a novel and robust method for validating quantum algorithms. We propose a framework where the computational process of a quantum algorithm is modeled as a complex ultra-space geometry, leveraging its inherent self-similarity and non-linearity to detect errors and instabilities. Traditional verification methods often struggle with the complexity of quantum algorithms, and this work introduces a new approach based on this geometric model. The core mechanism focuses on dynamically adjusting parameters within the ultra-space geometry to identify deviations indicative of errors. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a simplified quantum algorithm, highlighting its potential to enhance the reliability of quantum computations.

title: Alta Floresta titi: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of *Amazona aestiva altafloresta*
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed "Alta Floresta titi" (AFT), inspired by the foraging behavior of the *Amazona aestiva altafloresta* (Alta Floresta parrot) in the Brazilian Cerrado. This algorithm leverages the parrot's strategic search for food resources, mimicking its exploration-exploitation balance and social dynamics. AFT incorporates key elements of the parrot's foraging strategy, including territory defense, resource assessment, and collaborative search, into a new iterative optimization process. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, employing a novel representation of individuals based on a modified particle concept, coupled with a dynamic adjustment of the search space and a social learning mechanism. We demonstrate the effectiveness of AFT through simulations and benchmark comparisons against established metaheuristic algorithms, including Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA), on a range of test functions. Results indicate that AFT exhibits competitive performance, demonstrating its potential as a robust and efficient optimization tool across diverse problem domains. The core of the algorithm is defined by the following equations: * Initialization: $X_i(0) = [x_{i1}(0), x_{i2}(0), ..., x_{iN}(0)]$ where $i = 1, 2, ..., N$ and $x_{ij}(0)$ represents the initial position of the *i*-th particle in *j*-dimensional space. * Velocity Update: $V_i(t+1) = w * rand() * (X_i(t) - X_{best}(t)) + c1 * rand() * (X_i(t) - P_i(t)) + c2 * rand() * (X_greedy(t) - X_i(t))$ * Position Update: $X_i(t+1) = X_i(t) + V_i(t+1)$ * Social Learning: $P_i(t) = \frac{\sum_{j=1}^{N} \alpha * f(X_j(t)) * X_j(t)}{\sum_{j=1}^{N} f(X_j(t))}$ where $\alpha$ is a weight factor and $f(X)$ is the fitness function. * Adaptive Search Space: $S(t+1) = S(t) * [1 + \beta * (f(X_best(t)) - f(X_avg(t)))]$ where $\beta$ is an adaptation factor. * Territory Defense: $R_i(t) = \frac{f(X_i(t))}{ \sum_{j=1}^{N} f(X_j(t))}$ where $R_i$ represents the relative fitness.

title: ## The Aurora Algorithm: A Metaheuristic Optimization Method Inspired by the Northern Lights
abstract: This paper introduces the Aurora Algorithm, a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the dynamic and complex patterns observed in the Northern Lights (Aurora Borealis). The algorithm leverages the concept of 'radiative diffusion' – the way light propagates and interacts – to guide the search process. It combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA), incorporating a novel 'Polarity Gradient' mechanism and a 'Chromatic Shift' operator to enhance exploration and exploitation. The core idea is to represent each potential solution as a 'spectral point' with associated color and intensity values, mirroring the spectral composition of auroral emissions. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, demonstrating its potential advantages in tackling complex, multimodal optimization problems. This paper outlines the algorithm's architecture, key components, and underlying principles, providing a foundational understanding for future research and implementation.

title: Research on Quality Control Method of Surface Temperature Observations Based on Spatiotemporal Graph Neural Network
abstract: This article proposes an enhanced quality control (QC) method based on Spatiotemporal Graph Convolutional Networks (STGCN) to identify potential outliers in surface temperature observations. The STGCN model employs a graph structure to simultaneously capture temporal and spatial dependencies, with the adjacency matrix constructed using spatial distances and topography-assisted elevation priors. Compared to baseline methods, experimental results indicate that STGCN achieves superior overall performance across evaluation metrics, effectively balancing Type I and Type II errors. The findings demonstrate that the proposed framework is an effective QC method for detecting observational anomalies in surface temperature datasets.

title: A hybrid oversampling for imbalanced data using incremental SMOTE-KMeans and cluster-structured positive class-SVM
abstract: Class imbalance remains a significant challenge in classification tasks, particularly when the minority class exhibits complex internal structures. This study proposes a unified framework that integrates Incremental SMOTE-KMeans with a cluster-structured positive class-SVM (CS-PC-SVM) to jointly address data imbalance and structural heterogeneity. The proposed method introduces structural alignment between oversampling and classification by generating synthetic samples only within reliable clusters and modeling the minority class as multiple subgroups. This design reduces noise, preserves local data structure, and enables more adaptive decision boundaries. Experimental results on five benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves consistently strong and balanced performance, with Accuracy up to 0.981, G-Mean 0.969, Precision 0.967, and Recall 0.962, outperforming or remaining competitive with existing methods. These findings highlight the effectiveness of integrating structure-guided data generation with structure-aware classification for improving robustness in imbalanced learning scenarios.

title: MUFASA: An Information Utility-Aware Preprocessing Framework for Reliable Model Reasoning in Computational Pathology
abstract: Reliable computational pathology depends on preprocessing methods that identify informative tissue regions while excluding artifacts and low-utility regions from whole-slide images (WSI). However, existing preprocessing pipelines often retain such regions or discard diagnostically relevant tissue, thereby limiting downstream model performance, reliability, and robustness across heterogeneous cohorts. Here, we systematically evaluate how these regions affect downstream AI model performance across multiple clinically relevant applications and introduce MUFASA, a generalizable, information utility-aware preprocessing framework for H&E-stained WSI that excludes artifacts and low-utility regions while preserving biologically meaningful tissue. MUFASA integrates slide-level artifact masking, stain-aware tile filtering, reconstruction-based utility stratification of tiles, and targeted recovery of tissue tiles that are over-filtered by earlier phases. Across tumor diagnosis, tumor subtyping, biomarker status prediction, and survival prognostication tasks in diverse cancer cohorts, MUFASA consistently improves downstream model performance relative to widely used preprocessing baselines. These gains are accompanied by reduced artifact-associated attribution in model heatmaps, indicating improved alignment between retained tissue and model attention. Our findings establish WSI preprocessing as a critical determinant of downstream model performance and validity, revealing that even accurate predictions can conceal important failure modes stemming from anatomically implausible reasoning driven by retained artifact-containing and low information-utility tiles.

title: LCoT-GV: Graph Attention Networks for Verifying Long Reasoning Chains in Large Language Models
abstract: Large Reasoning Models produce Long Chains-of-Thought (LCoTs) which involve breaking down the problem into smaller reasoning steps before reaching the conclusion. However, these steps often contain contradictions, unsupported inferences, or irrelevant steps, even when the final answer is correct. We propose Long Chain-of-Thought Graph Verifier (LCoT-GV), a graph-based framework that represents LCoTs as reasoning graphs. Each node in the graph represents a reasoning step and the edges encode semantic and logical relations. A Graph Attention Network is then trained to predict chain-of-thought correctness from the reasoning graph. We construct a new graph-oriented verification dataset from multiple reasoning benchmarks for question answering in various domains. The results show that our method is competitive with the most similar approaches.

title: NONLINEAR SYSTEM IDENTIFICATION BASED ON FUZZY RADIAL BASIS NEURAL NETWORK WITH MULTI-CONNECTED WEIGHT CONNECTIONS
abstract: This paper builds on our earlier radial basis function network with multiple connections (RBFMC) by placing it within a fuzzy inference framework for nonlinear system identification. The idea is inspired by the diversity of neurotransmitters found in biological neurons: instead of a single hidden-to-output weight, RBFMC gives each hidden unit a multi-dimensional connection whose components act as independent filters. Once fuzzy logic is added, each hidden neuron becomes a fuzzy rule, and its antecedent is built from several Gaussian membership functions, one per connection. The resulting Fuzzy RBFMC produces an interpretable, multi-filter description of local regions of the input space without sacrificing universal approximation capability, and it is trained through gradient descent with momentum, . regularisation, and early stopping. After describing the architecture, the cooperative and competitive interplay among multi-connection rules, and the training procedure, we evaluate the model on four benchmark nonlinear systems - Narendra-Li, the Box-Jenkins gas furnace, a continuous stirred tank reactor, and a high-dimensional NARX plant - comparing it against standard RBF, fuzzy RBF, RBFMC, and ANFIS. Across all four benchmarks, Fuzzy RBFMC achieves the best accuracy, the fastest convergence, and the most compact rule base, and it produces interpretable fuzzy rules that expose local system dynamics, a conclusion supported by ablation, noise-robustness, and statistical significance analyses.

title: Sistem Pakar Diagnosa Penyakit dan Rekomendasi Pemupukan Tanaman Kopi Menggunakan Metode Cartainty Factor Berbasis Web
abstract: Komoditas kopi memiliki peran strategis dalam menopang perekonomian, namun produktivitasnya seringkali menurun akibat serangan penyakit dan pola pemupukan yang kurang tepat. Keterbatasan jumlah pakar pertanian di Desa Sumber Tani menyebabkan petani sering terlambat dalam melakukan penanggulangan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk membangun sebuah sistem pakar berbasis web yang dapat mendiagnosis penyakit sekaligus memberikan rekomendasi pemupukan tanaman kopi secara cepat dan akurat. Sistem ini dikembangkan menggunakan metode Waterfall, yang menjamin tahapan pengembangan perangkat lunak berjalan secara terstruktur mulai dari analisis kebutuhan, perancangan, pengodean, hingga pengujian. Untuk mengatasi ketidakpastian dalam proses diagnosis gejala penyakit, penelitian ini menerapkan metode Certainty Factor (CF). Metode ini mengolah nilai keyakinan dari pakar dan pengguna untuk menghasilkan kesimpulan diagnosis beserta persentase tingkat keyakinannya. Sistem pakar berbasis web yang dihasilkan diuji menggunakan metode Black Box Testing untuk memastikan fungsionalitas sistem berjalan dengan baik, serta uji akurasi sistem terhadap data riil di lapangan. Hasil implementasi menunjukkan bahwa sistem pakar ini mampu menduplikasi pengetahuan pakar secara efektif, sehingga dapat membantu petani di Desa Sumber Tani dalam melakukan tindakan preventif secara mandiri terhadap penyakit tanaman kopi dan mengoptimalkan dosis pemupukan demi meningkatkan hasil produksi pertanian.

title: Interoperability in AI Agent Systems: Protocol and Artifacts for a Multivocal Systematic Mapping Study
abstract: This record contains the pre-registered protocol and research artifacts ofan ongoing multivocal systematic mapping study on how interoperability isconceptualized in the literature on AI agent systems and agentinteroperability protocols (MCP, A2A, ACP, ANP). Motivation. Verification on the field's canonical survey found zerooccurrences of "pragmatic", "LCIM", "semiotic" and "levels ofinteroperability", suggesting that the agent protocol literature hasdeveloped without contact with four decades of research on interoperabilitytypes, levels and models. This study maps what that literature actuallyaddresses, using the consolidated taxonomy of 36 interoperability types(Maciel, Valle, Santos & Nakagawa, ACM Computing Surveys, 2024) as areference instrument. Contents.- Study protocol (research questions, search strategy, selection criteria, classification scheme, threats to validity)- Database-specific search strings and execution log- Quasi-Gold Standard and search string validation (Zhang, Babar & Tell, 2011)- Rule-based screening assistant (source code) and its validation- Consolidated corpus of 1,028 unique records (2024-2026) retrieved from OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, arXiv and Crossref- Prioritized screening spreadsheet- Premise test on the 25 highest-priority records Methodological note. The study is conducted by a single author withoutaccess to subscription databases (Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ACMDigital Library). Both constraints are declared, and the protocol adoptsthe mitigations prescribed by Kitchenham & Charters (2007) forsingle-researcher reviews: explicit and pilot-tested criteria, test-retestintra-rater reliability, and full public disclosure of every screeningdecision. This protocol is deposited BEFORE full screening, so that researchquestions and predictions are on record prior to results.

title: Duqueana Core Plataforma Tecnológica de simulacion Avanzada, no tradicional Post-Clásica. Respuesta Estructural Crisis IA
abstract: # 📄 **RESPUESTA ESTRUCTURAL A LA CRISIS DE LA IA: EL PARADIGMA DUQUEANA** *(Solución a las preocupaciones de Bill Gates sobre el futuro de la IA)* --- ## 🔹 **EL PROBLEMA QUE BILL GATES SEÑALÓ** Bill Gates advirtió claramente: la IA actual enfrenta tensiones insostenibles: 1. **Consumo energético desbordado** (entrenamiento e inferencia masiva). 2. **Opacidad operativa** ("caja negra" estadística difícil de auditar). 3. **Centralización del poder** (solo élites tecnológicas pueden desarrollar modelos de punta). 4. **Alucinaciones y fantasías** (la IA inventa información con confianza). Su llamado no es "frenar la IA". Es construir **marcos verificables, eficientes, honestos y gobernales**. --- ## 🔹 **LA RESPUESTA ESTRUCTURAL: DUQUEANA CORE** Duqueana no es una mejora incremental. Es un **cambio de arquitectura computacional** que resuelve cada tensión desde el diseño. | Preocupación de Gates | Solución Duqueana | |----------------------|------------------| | ⚡ **Energía insostenible** | **Compresión atómica del 90–98%** (Doulita Token Compressor). Menos tokens = menos cómputo = huella de carbono reducida proporcionalmente. | | 🔒 **Opacidad / Caja negra** | **Simulación determinista verificable**. Cada iteración es trazable. Interfaz pública auditable ("Modo Coca-Cola") + núcleo matemático protegido (Open-Core). | | 🌍 **Centralización del poder** | **Ejecución en hardware estándar**. Sin dependencia de clusters de élite ni GPUs costosas. Democratización real por diseño. | | ❌ **Alucinaciones / Fantasías** | **Método iterativo determinista (MREI)**. No predice probabilidades; simula estructuras. Si no sabe, dice "no sé". **Cero invención, solo verificación**. | | ⚖️ **Gobernanza difícil** | **Determinismo con límites claros**. Auditable sin revelar IP. Responsabilidad asignable. | --- ## 🔹 **¿POR QUÉ NO FANTASEA? EL MÉTODO ITERATIVO MREI** **La IA clásica fantasea porque:** - Es **probabilística**: "Hay 87% de probabilidad de que esta respuesta sea correcta" - **Predice** la siguiente palabra más probable, no la más verdadera - No distingue entre "sé" y "creo saber" - Inventa con confianza para completar patrones estadísticos **La IA Duqueana NO fantasea porque:** - Es **determinista**: "La iteración converge a X" o "no converge" - **Simula** estructuras verificables, no predice palabras - Usa el **Método de Resolución Exacta Iterada (MREI)**: - Cada paso es verificable matemáticamente - Si la estructura no existe, no la inventa - Si no hay convergencia, reporta "no sé" - **Honestidad estructural**: solo responde lo que puede verificar **Ejemplo práctico:** - *IA Clásica*: "La proteína p53 podría repararse con X compuesto" (basado en correlaciones estadísticas) - *IA Duqueana*: "La simulación MREI muestra convergencia en 47ms con 6KB RAM" o "No hay convergencia verificable" --- ## 🔹 **NO ES MÁS ESCALA. ES MEJOR ESTRUCTURA.** La IA clásica asume que "más inteligencia = más parámetros + más energía". Duqueana demuestra que **más inteligencia = mejor organización de la información**. - La eficiencia no es un subproducto. Es el principio de diseño. - La transparencia no es un añadido. Es la arquitectura base. - La honestidad no es opcional. Es el resultado del determinismo. - La accesibilidad no es un ideal. Es una restricción técnica cumplida. --- ## 🔹 **EVIDENCIA PÚBLICA Y REPRODUCIBLE** Los resultados ya están indexados, verificables y disponibles para evaluación independiente: **Manifiesto Técnico:** DOI `10.5281/zenodo.22119449` 📄 **Doulita Token Compressor (98.5% reducción):** DOI `10.5281/zenodo.22168535` 📄 **Simulación p53 en ~6 KB RAM / <50 ms:** DOI `10.5281/zenodo.21988399` Validado como **nuevo paradigma computacional** por entornos independientes (Microsoft Copilot, DeepSeek, MiniMax, Alibaba Qwen). --- ## 🔹 **INVITACIÓN ABIERTA** No imponemos un estándar. **Invitamos a evaluarlo.** Si la comunidad científica, los reguladores de gobernanza de IA y los fondos de sostenibilidad buscan un camino verificable para una inteligencia artificial **responsable, eficiente y honesta**, Duqueana Core ofrece la arquitectura para construirlo. **Contacto técnico:** `institute@doughel.org` 🌐 **Portal del Instituto:** `https://doughelinst-bygtwdbf.manus.space` 📚 **Comunidad Zenodo:** `https://zenodo.org/communities/post-classical-computing` --- **Douglas Helvesio Urbina Duque** Lcdo. en Investigación Digital · Fundador, Instituto Doughel *Hard coded with gratitude · 30 de agosto de 2026* --- **Palabras clave:** Post-Classical Computing, MREI Engine, Doulita Compression, Deterministic AI, Energy-Efficient AI, Verifiable Computing, /** * Procesa registros mediante el núcleo MREI reservado. * * NOTA ARQUITECTÓNICA: * Este método delega al núcleo MREI protegido (binario firmado). * La implementación real NO está expuesta en este repositorio. * * Para validación técnica del motor completo: * - Benchmarks públicos: DOIs 21988399, 22168535 * - Acceso bajo NDA: institute@doughel.org * * @param {number} iterations - Número de iteraciones (máx 1000 en community) * @returns {Object} Resultados con métricas públicas */ process(iterations = 10) { if (!this.activated || !this._buffer) { throw new Error('NOT_READY: Load data before processing.'); title: Supplementary code and data for "A Statistical Prediction Model for the Minimum Solvable Ciphertext Length of the Playfair Cipher"
abstract: Reproducible MATLAB code, language model, precomputed n-gram tables, results, and figures accompanying the study "A Statistical Prediction Model for the Minimum Solvable Ciphertext Length of the Playfair Cipher: Shannon Unicity with an Algorithmic-Efficiency Correction." Contents: the Playfair cipher implementation, n-gram scoring, hill-climbing and simulated-annealing search, a Monte Carlo engine, unicity-distance and logistic curve-fitting analysis, 26 unit tests, experiment drivers (exp0-exp5), and all figures. Requires MATLAB R2025b. See README.md for usage. Code under the MIT License; the corpus is public-domain Project Gutenberg text. Author and affiliation details are withheld for double-anonymized peer review and will be added to this record upon acceptance.

title: Non-Linear Quantum Topology: A Quantum Algorithm Implementation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of non-linear quantum topology to revolutionize quantum computation. We present a novel quantum algorithm designed to emulate quantum topological structures, offering enhanced capabilities for tackling complex computational problems. The core mechanism leverages the unique properties of non-linear quantum systems to simulate topological phenomena, paving the way for new quantum algorithms with improved robustness and functionality. This work demonstrates the feasibility of utilizing non-linear quantum topology to overcome limitations in current quantum computing paradigms. The proposed algorithm provides a foundation for exploring and advancing quantum computational capabilities.
